jobs.title: Customer Service Generalist
jobs.description_html:
General Description

The Customer Experience Generalist plays a key role in supporting the Customer Service department across diversefunctions, including Collections, Dispatch, Billing, and the Call Center. This dynamic and adaptable position requires aproactive, customer-focused professional capable of navigating shifting priorities while consistently upholdingexceptional service standards and embodying the Toho Promise. This role is essential in driving operational efficiencyand ensuring seamless, high-quality customer experience. This position will work collaboratively with multiplesupervisors across various functions. The individual will engage with the appropriate supervisor(s) depending on theassigned tasks and responsibilities, ensuring effective coordination and support from all relevant parties.

Essential Functions

1. Adapt to various roles, following departmental procedures, and shift focus based on urgent needs to ensureseamless operations.
2. Maintain clear and professional communication with customers, field staff, and internal teams to support smoothcoordination and timely updates.
3. Prioritize tasks, troubleshoot issues, and complete work in a timely manner while ensuring accuracy and qualityacross all functions.
4. Suggest and implement process improvements to enhance operational efficiency while ensuring compliance with Toho policies and regulations.

Minimum Qualifications

1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
2. Minimum 2 years' relevant experience.
3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully inthis position will be considered.
4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:
1. Exceptional organizational skills with a high level of attention to detail, ensuring thorough follow-through andprofessionalism under pressure.
2. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part ofa team.
3. Proven ability to manage projects, multitask, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines in fast-paced environments.
4. Sound judgment and discretion, with the ability to maintain confidentiality of sensitive information and documents.
5. Proactive, resourceful, and flexible, with a positive attitude and confidence to take initiative, make decisions, andadapt within established guidelines.
6. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and familiarity with CIS, meter datasystems, and payment portal systems (preferred).
7. Excellent verbal and written communication skills, paired with strong problem-solving abilities to de-escalatechallenging situations effectively.
8. High attention to detail and accuracy in data entry, record-keeping, and overall task execution.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoors, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Customer Experience Advocate - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Customer Experience Advocate I $25.60-$34.08
Senior Customer Experience Advocate $27.36-$36.45

The primary purpose of this position is to case manage complex customer situations to improve the customer experience. This position will track customer inquiries as they are worked throughout the organization and provides closed loop communication with the customer. These individuals will also handle written responses to customers resulting from both email and social media inquiries. This position will be highly networked within Toho and work closely with internal and external partners to resolve customer concerns. This position reports to a Customer Experience Supervisor.

Essential Functions

The duties and responsibilities listed below are intended to provide a representative list of the various types of work that may be performed. Specifications are not intended to reflect all duties performed within the job class, and incumbents may expect to perform other related similar duties. Some of the duties include, but are not limited to, the following.

  1. Demonstrate excellent teamwork, communication, and customer service skills in a fast-paced environment to help address complex and sensitive inquiries
  2. Case manage complex customer situations and deliver a seamless customer experience.
  3. Efficiently utilize software programs for data entry, retrieval, review and track and maintain communication with customers for long lead time resolutions.
  4. Partner with Operations to address escalated/repeated water quality concerns received from customers.
  5. Research and respond (off-line) to social media inquiries – both Google Reviews and those received via PIO.
  6. Research and respond to customer or community inquiries received by Executive Director, Board Members or other elected officials.
  7. Respond to messages received to the Toho Customer Service email address.
  8. Process estimated billing tier adjustment requests / escalations and new service applications.
  9. Provide closed loop communication on customer-initiated Technician calls.
  10. Perform periodic supervisory duties as needed.
  11. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  3. Minimum of 5 years’ experience in customer service with preference applied to experience obtained within a utility.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:
  1. Ability to build relationships and maintain a strong network of subject matter experts.
  2. Confidence to be proactive and take initiative, make decisions and change course within established guidelines.
  3. Strong organization and follow-thru skills; detail oriented with the ability to maintain professionalism under pressure
  4. Strong people skills, including the ability to work effectively as part of a team.
  5. Proven ability to exercise sound, independent judgement and discretion while maintaining confidentiality of information and documents
  6. Positive attitude and the ability to be proactive, resourceful and flexible
  7. Working knowledge of Microsoft Suite of products (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  8. Strong verbal and written communication skills
  9. Demonstrate ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Billing Specialist - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Under general supervision, performs a variety of billing and customer account functions to ensure accurate, complete, and timely processing of billing services. Responsibilities include researching billing issues, maintaining customer account information, and resolving billing-related inquiries. This position requires professionalism, tact, and courtesy when interacting with customers and the general public. The position reports directly to the Billing/Collections Manager.

Essential Functions

  1. Demonstrates a basic understanding of customer account management and billing principles, with strong attention to detail and accuracy. 
  2. Reviews, researches, and prepares customer accounts for billing, including reviewing exception reports, correcting billing errors, processing manual adjustments, and ensuring accurate application of rates and fees. 
  3. Verifies meter reads are accurately imported into the billing system, maintains meter inventory and meter activity, and troubleshoots AMI meter-reading exceptions, including creating service orders when field repairs are needed. 
  4. Prepares and monitors daily utility billing cycles, creates appropriate billing batches, reviews billing exceptions, and performs quality control to ensure timely and accurate billing. 
  5. Reviews completed service orders and account records to ensure appropriate charges are applied and calculates adjustments for transfers, initial and final bills, rate changes, fees, and other account activity. 
  6. Assists with customer account inquiries and clearly explains billing methods, rates, fees, charges, payments, and available payment options. 
  7. Uses Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, Outlook, and Word, and demonstrates the ability to learn utility billing software and other business systems. 
  8. Communicates effectively and professionally with customers, coworkers, and the public while providing excellent customer service. 
  9. Prioritizes assignments, meets deadlines, and works effectively both independently and as part of a team in a fast-paced environment. 
  10. Provides input on the development and revision of Standard Operating Procedures and billing procedures and performs other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of education and experience demonstrating the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered. 

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. One (1) year of banking, customer service, clerical, administrative support, cash handling, data entry, or related experience.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Experience working in utility billing, accounts receivable, finance, or customer service environments.
  1. Familiarity with computerized billing or customer information systems.
  2. Experience with Microsoft Excel and data management.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Plant Mechanic (Preventative Maintenance) - I, II, Senior, Master
jobs.description_html:
General Description


Salary:
  Plant Mechanic I: $22.34 - $27.91 Hourly
 Plant Mechanic II: $25.60 - $34.08 Hourly
 Senior Plant Mechanic: $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
 Master Plant Mechanic: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly
The purpose of this position is to support the reliable and efficient operation of Water and/or Wastewater Treatment Facilities through predictive, preventive, and corrective maintenance of plant systems and equipment. This position is responsible for monitoring equipment condition, identifying early indicators of mechanical failure, and implementing maintenance strategies that maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime. Duties include diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing, and replacing a variety of pumps, motors, valves, and other mechanical equipment; analyzing equipment performance trends; and recommending repairs, upgrades, and maintenance schedules to extend asset life and improve operational performance. 
The ideal candidate is passionate about equipment reliability and proactive maintenance. They possess a strong mechanical aptitude and experience maintaining critical treatment facility equipment, including pumps, motors, valves, gearboxes, and related systems. They are skilled in predictive maintenance techniques such as vibration analysis, lubrication management, condition monitoring, precision alignment, and equipment performance trending. The candidate can effectively diagnose mechanical issues, identify early indicators of failure, and implement maintenance strategies that improve asset reliability, reduce downtime, and extend equipment life. They communicate effectively across operations and maintenance teams, maintain accurate records within the CMMS, and are committed to safety, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

Essential Functions

Plant Mechanic I:

  1. Repairs and replaces various equipment by utilizing truck cranes, hand tools, and electrical meters; locking out tag out; removing debris from impeller and volutes; monitoring motor oil, power cords, bells; assessing conditions; and performing monthly PM's.
  2. Troubleshoots for errors by monitoring meg and ohm motors; checking electrical voltages, components, wiring, and connections; checking floats and transducers; and utilizing Schematic diagrams.
  3. Maintains generators and performs administrative work by conducting preventative maintenance; installing by pass and generators; hooking up power cables; assisting on vac trucks; checking e-mails and SCADA readings; creating work orders; attending monthly safety meetings; and overseeing pagers, phones, and radios.
  4. Manages confined spaces by utilizing gas monitors, oxygen tanks, tripods, etc.; calibrating gas monitors; repairing and changing rails; disposing of debris; changing pipes; and repairing brackets and check valves.
  5. Maintains trucks by inspecting vehicles, lights, gauges, tires, tools, oils, belts, etc.; and inspecting cranes.
  6. All other duties as assigned.

Plant Mechanic II:

  1. Repairs and replaces various equipment by utilizing truck cranes, hand tools, and electrical meters; locking out tag out; removing debris from impellor and volutes; monitoring motor oil, power cords, bells; assessing conditions; and performing monthly PM's.
  2. Troubleshoots for errors by back-flushing check valves; monitoring meg and ohm motors; checking electrical voltages, components, wiring, and connections; checking floats and transducers; and utilizing Schematic diagrams.
  3. Performs administrative work by checking e-mails; overseeing SCADA readings; creating work orders; attending monthly safety meetings and training events; managing credit card statements; supervising pagers and radios; analyzing spill reports and root causes; and creating stand-by and weekend report timesheets.
  4. Performs inspections by checking exit lights and fire extinguishers; overseeing equipment, trucks, and crane; checking confine space trailer equipment; and inspections warehouse and MCC alarm systems.
  5. All other duties as assigned.

Senior Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Understand the principles and processes involved in water and wastewater treatment, including filtration, sedimentation, disinfection, and chemical treatment.
  2. Familiarity with Toho Water standards and specifications, ensuring all equipment meets criteria.
  3. Ability to identify the need for and to submit GIS red lines for system updates.
  4. Ability to analyze data from monitoring equipment and make adjustments to optimize plant performance and efficiency.
  5. Demonstrate proficiency in welding and fabrication techniques to repair or members are informed and compliant with safety regulations.
  6. Proficiency in using computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) and other software tools for scheduling maintenance, managing inventory, and documenting work activities.
  7. Demonstrate expertise in performing precision shaft alignment to ensure accurate alignment between motors, pumps, gearboxes, and other machinery components to reduce vibration, prevent premature wear, and extend equipment life in accordance with manufacturer specifications and industry standards.
  8. Identify need for confined space entry. Demonstrate understanding of procedures and oversee a team in performing confined space entry, ensuring adherence to safety protocols and regulations.
  9. Demonstrate an understanding of plumbing principles and the ability to work with pipes, fitting, and fixtures to ensure proper installation and functionality.
  10. Demonstrate proficiency in completing pre-hurricane preparation (72 hours prior) and level III hurricane response (36 hours prior) checklists, including placement of generators/bypass pumps for optimal response.
  11. Ability to effectively communicate with team members, supervisors and other stakeholders to coordinate tasks, report findings, and collaborate on projects.
  12. Identify training needs, develop and deliver a training presentation to the department.
  13. Demonstrate skill in handling escalated situations with customers/contractors effectively, maintaining professionalism and resolving issues promptly.

Master Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Demonstrate ability to effectively lead and coordinate a crew, delegating tasks and ensuring efficient workflow.
  2. Demonstrate proficiency in assigning work orders and generating preventative maintenance tasks within INFOR or CityWorks system.
  3. Demonstrate understanding or incident reporting protocols and procedures. Ability to accurately complete supervisor incident reports.
  4. Demonstrate understanding of payroll processes and procedures within ADP. Ability to effectively validate timesheets for payroll purposes.
  5. Proficient in interpreting and comprehending construction and engineering drawings. Demonstrate ability to accurately interpret plan designs for maintenance and repair tasks.

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.

Plant Mechanic II:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of three years relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control.

This position is responsible for monitoring equipment condition, identifying early indicators of mechanical failure, and implementing maintenance strategies that maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime. jobs.description_html:
General Description

Service Technician I $19.50 - $24.38 (Hourly)
 Service Technician II $20.87 - $26.08 (Hourly)
 Service Technician III $22.34 - $27.91 (Hourly)
Service Technician I General Description:
The Service Technician I is an entry level position in the Customer Service Department. The role of this position is to provide field customer service by performing tasks associated with physically initiating and discontinuing water service, leak investigation and various customer service functions.  The purpose of this position is to provide accurate information for billing of utility services and professional customer service assistance to citizens and business owners, and to perform a variety of maintenance and customer service tasks on residential and commercial water meters.
Service Technician II General Description:
The purpose of this position is to provide field customer service to and guide customer bases. This is accomplished by communicating with customers; evaluating repairs; replaying to inquiries; directing bi-weekly meetings; and ensuring team performs regular vehicle checks. Other duties include changing and replacing meters; evaluating and solving issues with AMI programs; repairing leaks; maintaining supplies and inventory; overseeing vehicle checks; and training new team members.  In addition, oversee reconnection of service and disconnection of service at customer sites. The successful candidate will have demonstrated an ability to provide excellent customer service, strong communication skills, ability to respond professionally to difficult intensified conflicts, and teamwork skills. Preference will be given to applicants with familiarity of Toho Water Authority's service area.
Service Technician III General Description:
The role of this position is to provide field customer service. This is accomplished by communicating with internal and external customers; accurately completing work orders, routing daily work using navigation sources and prioritization of tickets based on urgency level, and performing water quality tests.  In addition, install remote meters, complete small commercial disconnects, and maintain or install a DCU.

Essential Functions

Service Technician I Essential Functions:

  1. Provide customer service internally and externally.
  2. Complete work orders and associated paperwork accurately and in a timely manner.
  3. Plan work and schedule route using navigation system and service area mapping.
  4. Inspect work truck and maintain inventory and supplies in work truck.
  5. Internally and externally communicates with customers by meeting and responding to customers; advising customer of resolution; completing work paperwork accurately; connecting with internal customer; visiting work sites; communicating with team members and maintaining inventory and supplies.
  6. Disconnect and reconnect meters using proper tools and within timelines and deadlines.
  7. Accesses and enters data or information using a personal computer.
  8. Performs miscellaneous work by assisting with collection activities i.e. disconnect, reconnect, tampering, broken promises, NSF's etc.; exposing curb stops; digging up meters; and maintaining supplies and inventory.
  9. Other duties as assigned.
Service Technician II Essential Functions:
  1. Internally and externally communicates with customers by meeting and responding to customers; advising customer of resolution; fulfilling paperwork; connecting with internal customer; visiting work sites; communicating with team members; maintaining inventory and supplies; and communicating with team on emergency needs. 
  2. Replaces meters, boxes, and lids by exchanging meters; ensuring accuracy of organization revenue source; digging out meter boxes; replacing meter gaskets; reprogramming devices; fulfilling paperwork; and visiting work sites. 
  3. Repairs AMI system by replacing and reprogramming devices; checking for water leaks; corresponding with customers about leaks; and visiting work sites. 
  4. Installs new meters by collecting paperwork; scheduling in accordance with order of payment and subdivision; guaranteeing proper materials are on vehicle; replacing curb stop and meter connector; digging out meter taps; installing and programming devices; and completing paperwork. 
  5. Tests water meters by performing bench tests; visiting work sites; replacing and installing meters; documenting meter accuracy; fulfilling paperwork; and testing flow for water meters. 
  6. Tests water meters by performing bench tests; visiting work sites; replacing and installing meters; documenting meter accuracy; fulfilling paperwork; and testing flow for water meters.
     Performs miscellaneous work by assisting with collection activities; exposing curb stops; digging up meters; and maintaining supplies and inventory.
  7. All other duties as assigned. 
Service Technician III Essential Functions:
  1. Provide customer service internally and externally. 
  2. Complete work orders and associated paperwork accurately and in a timely manner. 
  3. Plan work and schedule route using navigation system and service area mapping. 
  4. Inspect work truck and maintain inventory and supplies in work truck. 
  5. Internally and externally communicates with customers by meeting and responding to customers; advising customer of resolution; completing work paperwork accurately; connecting with internal customer; visiting work sites; communicating with team members and maintaining inventory and supplies. 
  6. Install and maintain DCU, set meter boxes and lids, read magnetic flow meters, complete small commercial disconnects per guidelines, and troubleshoot low pressure in the water system. 
  7. Performs miscellaneous work by assisting with collection activities i.e. disconnect, reconnect, tampering, broken promises, NSF's etc.; exposing curb stops; digging up meters; and maintaining supplies and inventory.
  8. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Service Technician I Minimum Qualifications:
Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. This is an entry level position; previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License
Service Technician II Minimum Qualifications: 
Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of one-year relevant experience. 
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
Service Technician III Minimum Qualifications: 
Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of two years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License. 
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain a Class B Driver's License within the first six months of employment.

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear.   5. Performs inspections by checking exit lights and fire extinguishers; overseeing equipment, trucks, and crane; checking confine space trailer equipment; and inspections warehouse and MCC alarm systems.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. This is an entry level position; previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's license.
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain Class B (CDL) Driver's License within the first six months of employment.

Systems Mechanic I:
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of one-year work experience with a focus on pump, motors, and/or controls.
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License. 
  5. A CDL Class A with Hazmat License is preferred but not required.

Systems Mechanic II:
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of three years relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. As a condition of employment, must obtain State of Florida Class A Driver's License within first six months of employment.

Senior Systems Mechanic:
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of three years relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. Class A CDL with applicable endorsement(s) as a required to be obtained within first six months of employment and maintained throughout employment

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Procurement Coordinator - I, II or Senior
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Procurement Coordinator I ($29.26 - $39.02) Hourly
Procurement Coordinator II ($32.77 - $46.82) Hourly
Senior Procurement Coordinator ($76,378 - $109,096) Annually

Join Toho Water Authority as a Procurement Coordinator and help shape the future of public procurement! We’re excited to announce one opportunity for a Procurement Coordinator, which may be filled at the I, II, or Senior level depending on the selected candidate’s experience and qualifications. In this role, you’ll support a diverse range of impactful projects in Engineering, Construction, Environmental, Compliance, and Safety. The ideal candidate will bring years of Florida Government Procurement experience, along with specialized knowledge in these key areas. Become part of a collaborative team that values innovation, transparency, and excellence in service to our community.


GENERAL DESCRIPTION:

Procurement Coordinator I
 The Procurement Coordinator I supports the success of all Toho stakeholders and is responsible for ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies while facilitating cost-effective, timely, and high-quality work to procure a variety of goods and services. Procurements may include analyzing quotes, sole source, piggybacks, and invitations for bids from inception to award. This role requires exceptional organizational and communication skills, collaborative teamwork skills, and a working knowledge and understanding of public procurement processes and industry best practices. Under direct supervision of a Senior Coordinator or Procurement Supervisor, the Procurement Coordinator I functions at entry-mid level to perform detailed work in the preparation, research, writing, evaluating and administration of bids and contracts. Work involves communication with vendors and departmental officials on purchasing problems and shipping, receiving, and invoicing problems and processes; and may include supporting p-card administration and oversight. Procurement Coordinators may manage multiple projects and deadlines simultaneously.
 
Procurement Coordinator II
 The Procurement Coordinator II supports the success of all Toho Water Authority stakeholders and is responsible for ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies while facilitating cost-effective, timely, and high-quality work to procure a variety of goods and services. This role requires exceptional organizational and communication skills, collaborative teamwork skills, and a working knowledge and understanding of public procurement processes and industry best practices. Under direct supervision of a Senior Coordinator or Procurement Supervisor, the Procurement Coordinator II functions at journey professional level to perform complex procurement services, analysis, and implement process improvement solutions. The role supports Toho Water Authority staff with procuring a wide variety of commodities and services using various solicitation methods including ITB/RFP/RFQu and alternate delivery methods of construction such as Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) or other strategies. The work involves leading all phases of the procurement process, from bid preparation through granting of the award for procurement and contract management including extensions, amendments and facilitating vendor performance issues. The Procurement Coordinator II will also contribute to the team by sharing knowledge and implementing continuous improvement strategies and processes with peers. Work is performed according to Toho Water Authority procurement guidelines, State of Florida laws, and any applicable federal laws and regulations to include requirements of grant agreements.
 Senior Procurement Coordinator
 The Senior Procurement Coordinator is a seasoned and highly skilled procurement professional relied upon as subject matter expert. The Senior Coordinator may function as an individual contributor or as a lead for a team of procurement coordinators, making assignments, providing guidance and ensuring the efficient execution of procurement strategies, and driving optimal cost savings while maintaining high-quality standards. This role requires analytical abilities, collaborative skills, and a deep understanding of procurement processes and industry best practices. The Senior Procurement Coordinator performs complex procurements, advice and guidance, delivery, and process improvement solutions to support Toho Water Authority. This is accomplished by developing and overseeing solicitation packages, contracts planning, analyzing proposals and determining contract strategies, evaluating bid and proposals for technical compliance, developing and monitoring project management timelines, and coordinating contract specifications. This position is responsible for handling the more complex procurements, problem solving and mediating of challenging or unexpected problems involving multiple stakeholders and departments. Senior Coordinators may be assigned to lead and/or represent Procurement as subject matter experts in cross functional continuous improvement project teams. The Senior Procurement Coordinator may be assigned day-to-day oversight of entry and mid-level coordinators to gain leadership and supervisory experience.

Essential Functions

Procurement Coordinator I
 

  1. Performs routine procurement work according to generally accepted public procurement principles, best practices, established procedures, departmental guidelines, and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
  2. Prepares, reviews, and processes standard documents, including solicitations, sole source, piggyback, including addenda, contract award and purchase orders, to include all contractual requirements and specifications.
  3. Schedules and facilitates pre-bid conferences, public formal bid and proposal openings; receives and analyzes bids and proposals received for conformance with specifications and other requirements.
  4. Uses e-procurement platform and financial management software to create or review and investigate any vendor records, department requisitions for purchase orders; includes contract set-up and spend summary maintenance; verifies items and prices and approves requisitions for purchase order issue.
  5. Monitors the status of assigned contracts with staff to prepare for timely renewals, contract extensions or new solicitations.
  6. Serves as primary contact with departments and outside agencies for the purpose of obtaining procurement information, purchase order authorization; as primary contact between departments and vendors/bidders for various commodities and services.
  7. Performs various administrative support duties, e.g. filing materials, copying documentation, entering data into computer system tasks and may include oversight for the procurement card (P-Card) program including issuing new cards, reports, training and monitoring for compliance.
  8. Maintains and updates procurement templates, SOP’s, Project tracker, cost savings reports, and other department tools as needed.
  9. Collaborates with staff advising on procurement procedures and managing solicitations and contracts.
  10. All other duties as assigned.

Procurement Coordinator II
 

  1. Fully master and perform all responsibilities and tasks outlined in the Procurement Coordinator I job description, demonstrating proficiency and independence in each area.
  2. Performs routine procurement work according to generally accepted public procurement principles, best practices, established procedures, departmental guidelines, and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
  3. Prepares complex bid and proposal documents to include all contractual requirements and specifications received from the end user; utilizes the automated procurement system with good judgment and understanding of the commodity codes, to determine vendors from whom to solicit bids and proposals; assignments require critical thinking and independent judgment carried out within the guidelines of established policies and procedures.
  4. Monitors the status of assigned contracts with staff to prepare for timely renewals or new solicitations; analyzes requests for price increases and contract extensions; confers with departments regarding specifications and updates when preparing solicitations.
  5. Facilitates pre-bid and pre-proposal conferences; conducts public formal bid openings and proposal closings; receives and analyzes bid proposals received for conformance with specifications and other requirements; initiates the approval process and procurement award to the Board and Executive Staff from the department or evaluation committee’s recommendation.
  6. Conducts review and approval of purchase orders in a timely manner.
  7. Serves as primary contact to Toho’s departments and outside agencies for the purpose of obtaining purchase order authorization for commodities and services; as primary contact between Toho’s departments and vendors/bidders for various commodities and services.
  8. Reviews sole source procurement requests to determine if all legal requirements have been met; analyzes quotations received for small procurements.
  9. Uses e-procurement platform and financial management software for solicitations, purchase orders and contract management.
  10. For Professional Services solicitations under Florida 287.055, ensures that all projects and documents fall within the Consultant’s Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA) guidelines.
  11. Collaborates with Toho Water Authority staff advising on procurement procedures and managing solicitations and contracts.
  12. Facilitates meetings with staff and vendors to address contract performance issues and creates documentation of results.
  13. Ensure Toho’s procurement practices fall within compliance guidelines for use of Federal and State Grants, Loans, etc.
  14. All other duties as assigned.


Senior Procurement Coordinator
 

  1. The role of the Senior Procurement Coordinator includes and may perform all the essential functions of the Procurement Coordinator positions.
  2. Implements effective procurement strategies and processes, optimizing cost savings, supplier management, and contract negotiation. Recommends, develops, and implements improved process methods and procedures.
  3. Monitors and analyzes procurement data, trends, and metrics to identify opportunities for process improvement and cost reduction.
  4. Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including finance, operations, and legal, to align procurement strategies with overall organizational goals.
  5. Provides a high level of service to internal and external customers while effectively resolving inquiries and challenges.
  6. Evaluate and select suppliers based on predefined criteria, negotiate contracts, and manage supplier relationships to ensure the highest quality and value for the organization.
  7. Conduct market research and stay updated on industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices to drive innovation and continuous improvement in procurement processes.
  8. Establish and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, both internal and external, to understand their needs, provide strategic advice, and influence decision-making processes.
  9. Ensure compliance with procurement regulations, standards, and requirements.
  10. Prepares and presents reports, performance metrics, and analysis to stakeholders, highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations.
  11. Manage multiple projects, facilitates award of contracts, ensures vendor insurance compliance and verification of contractor licenses.
  12. Collaborate with departments to establish goals and timelines for projects, pre-qualification and proposal evaluations.
  13. Solicit procurements by preparing documents, determining procurement strategies for projects including proposals and professional services, managing solicitation process, conducing pre-proposal and other public meetings; bid openings, contributing to contract negotiations, preparing correspondence, and processes materials/supplies as needed.
  14. Reviews and advice on scope of work for RFP's, participates in the evaluation and selection of vendors and contractors, and proactively monitors contract expirations. Supports departments in monitoring contract budgets.
  15. May function as a lead for entry and mid-level procurement staff providing training, delegation of assignments, and direct and review the work of others for compliance and development opportunities.
  16. Perform duties as assigned/necessary which are related, or logical in assignment to the position.
  17. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be:

Procurement Coordinator I
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of three years of relevant experience. Such as working in public sector procurement or contract administration; experience in Florida public sector procurement highly preferred. 
  3. Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet etc.) or similar platforms. 
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid state of Florida Class E Driver's License.
Procurement Coordinator II
  1. A minimum of 2-year college degree with a focus on Business Administration, Public Administration, Supply Chain Management or related field.
  2. Five years of experience working in a public sector procurement or contract administration.
  3. Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet Etc.)
  4. Must possess a professional purchasing-related certification such asCertified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) or Certified Procurement Professional (NICP-CPP) or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Certified Purchasing Manager (C.P.M.) or other relevant credential approved by Toho Procurement Leadership. 
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
Senior Procurement Coordinator 
  1. Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or related field.
  2. Minimum of five years’ experience working in public sector procurement or contract administration.
  3. Proven experience in procurement analysis, contract negotiation, and supplier management.  
  4. Three years of supervisory experience or experience in leading project teams. 
  5. Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform such as OpenGov/Bonfire/Bidnet, SAP, and Oracle. 
  6. Must possess a professional purchasing related certification such as Certified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) Certified Professional Public Officer (CPPO); Certified Procurement Professional (CPP) or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Certified Purchasing Manager (C.P.M) or other credential approved by Toho Procurement Leadership.   
  7. Must possess and maintain a valid state of Florida Class E Driver's License.

DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience in Florida Public Sector procurement.
  • Experience managing multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Experience with Requests for Proposals and other types of procurements – GSA/Cooperative Contracts, etc. especially in the areas of IT, Finance, HR, and Legal. 
  • Extensive knowledge of procurement processes, strategic sourcing, and supplier relationship management.
  • P-Card program administration, management and implementation, and Certified Procurement Card Professional (CPCP) highly desirable.
  • Experience in developing and presenting training to procurement and organization staff.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES

  1. Basic knowledge of public purchasing and general accounting principles and techniques.
  2. Skill in performing routine to moderately complex mathematical computations and tabulations accurately and efficiently; intermediate level business mathematics, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages and decimals.
  3. Ability to perform in accordance with pre-established local, State, and Federal policies, procedures and regulatory requirements applicable to the work.
  4. Ability to effectively communicate both orally and in writing.
  5. Ability to utilize personal computers, standard office equipment and standard software applications, e.g., word processors, database software, spreadsheet applications.
  6. Ability to read and interpret technical and legal documents, operation and maintenance instructions, and policy and procedure manuals.
  7. Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with unit employees, employees in other departments, public/private sector contacts, vendors, and the general public.
  8. Ability to maintain effective records maintenance and file management systems.
  9. Ability to organize work, establish priorities, meet established deadlines, and follow up on assignments with a minimum direction.
  10. Skill in preparing complex correspondence, summaries and reports in a clear and concise manner; skill in business English, e.g., correspondence formats, spelling, punctuation and grammar.
  11. Ability to access, operate and maintain various software applications.
  12. Skill in reading, updating and maintaining various records and files; skill in complex administrative support functions, e.g., records maintenance, data analysis, reports processing, documentation proofing.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to handle or feel and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk and bend, kneel, squat, or crawl. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

 Monitors the status of assigned contracts with staff to prepare for timely renewals or new solicitations; analyzes requests for price increases and contract extensions; confers with departments regarding specifications and updates when preparing solicitations.
 Facilitates pre-bid and pre-proposal conferences; conducts public formal bid openings and proposal closings; receives and analyzes bid proposals received for conformance with specifications and other requirements; initiates the approval process and procurement award to the Board and Executive Staff from the department or evaluation committee’s recommendation.
 Conducts review and approval of purchase orders in a timely manner.
 Serves as primary contact to Toho’s departments and outside agencies for the purpose of obtaining purchase order authorization for commodities and services; as primary contact between Toho’s departments and vendors/bidders for various commodities and services.
 Reviews sole source procurement requests to determine if all legal requirements have been met; analyzes quotations received for small procurements.
 Uses e-procurement platform and financial management software for solicitations, purchase orders and contract management.
 For Professional Services solicitations under Florida 287.055, ensures that all projects and documents fall within the Consultant’s Competitive Negotiation Act (CCNA) guidelines.
 Collaborates with Toho Water Authority staff advising on procurement procedures and managing solicitations and contracts.
 Facilitates meetings with staff and vendors to address contract performance issues and creates documentation of results.
 Ensure Toho’s procurement practices fall within compliance guidelines for use of Federal and State Grants, Loans, etc.
 All other duties as assigned.
 Senior Procurement Coordinator 
 The role of the Senior Procurement Coordinator includes and may perform all the essential functions of the Procurement Coordinator positions.
 Implements effective procurement strategies and processes, optimizing cost savings, supplier management, and contract negotiation. Recommends, develops, and implements improved process methods and procedures.
 Monitors and analyzes procurement data, trends, and metrics to identify opportunities for process improvement and cost reduction.
 Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including finance, operations, and legal, to align procurement strategies with overall organizational goals.
 Provides a high level of service to internal and external customers while effectively resolving inquiries and challenges.
 Evaluate and select suppliers based on predefined criteria, negotiate contracts, and manage supplier relationships to ensure the highest quality and value for the organization.
 Conduct market research and stay updated on industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices to drive innovation and continuous improvement in procurement processes.
 Establish and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, both internal and external, to understand their needs, provide strategic advice, and influence decision-making processes.
 Ensure compliance with procurement regulations, standards, and requirements.
 Prepares and presents reports, performance metrics, and analysis to stakeholders, highlighting achievements, challenges, and recommendations.
 Manage multiple projects, facilitates award of contracts, ensures vendor insurance compliance and verification of contractor licenses.
 Collaborate with departments to establish goals and timelines for projects, pre-qualification and proposal evaluations.
 Solicit procurements by preparing documents, determining procurement strategies for projects including proposals and professional services, managing solicitation process, conducing pre-proposal and other public meetings; bid openings, contributing to contract negotiations, preparing correspondence, and processes materials/supplies as needed.
 Reviews and advice on scope of work for RFP's, participates in the evaluation and selection of vendors and contractors, and proactively monitors contract expirations. Supports departments in monitoring contract budgets.
 May function as a lead for entry and mid-level procurement staff providing training, delegation of assignments, and direct and review the work of others for compliance and development opportunities.
 Perform duties as assigned/necessary which are related, or logical in assignment to the position.
 All other duties as assigned.
 Minimum Qualifications
 Any combination of training and experience that would provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities is qualifying. A typical way to obtain that required qualification would be: 
 Procurement Coordinator I A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
 Minimum of three years of relevant experience. Such as working in public sector procurement or contract administration; experience in Florida public sector procurement highly preferred. 
 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet etc.) or similar platforms. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid state of Florida Class E Driver's License.
 Procurement Coordinator II 
 A minimum of 2-year college degree with a focus on Business Administration, Public Administration, Supply Chain Management or related field.
 Five years of experience working in a public sector procurement or contract administration.
 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform (OpenGov/Bonfire/BidNet Etc.)
 Must possess a professional purchasing-related certification such asCertified Professional Public Buyer (CPPB) or Certified Procurement Professional (NICP-CPP) or Certified Professional in Supply Management (CPSM) or Certified Purchasing Manager (C.P.M.) or other relevant credential approved by Toho Procurement Leadership. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

 Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Finance, or related field.
 Minimum of five years’ experience working in public sector procurement or contract administration.

 Experience using financial software applications for contracts/purchase orders and an e-procurement platform such as OpenGov/Bonfire/Bidnet, SAP, and Oracle.

jobs.title: Business Process Specialist - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description

Business Process Specialist I: $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
Business Process Specialist II: $29.26 - $39.02 Hourly
Senior Business Process Specialist: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly

The Business Process Specialist is responsible for analyzing, documenting, modeling, and improving business processes across the organization to enhance operational efficiency, service quality, and organizational effectiveness. This role works closely with the Business Transformation Manager to facilitate process discovery workshops, develop process models using BPMN standards, identify improvement opportunities, and support the implementation of process changes.

The Business Process Specialist will work closely with the business stakeholders to document and improve processes across the entire enterprise. He/ she will serve as a bridge between business units and technology teams, ensuring that business requirements, process documentation, and improvement initiatives are effectively aligned with organizational objectives. While the primary focus of the role is process management and continuous improvement, the position also supports technology-related initiatives by collaborating with IT teams, reviewing system impacts, and helping translate business needs into functional requirements as and when necessary.

The ideal candidate is passionate about understanding how work gets done and helping teams improve it. They are comfortable leading process modeling workshops, documenting workflows using BPMN standards, applying Lean Six Sigma techniques, and partnering with both business and technology teams to deliver sustainable process improvements. They can effectively facilitate conversations, challenge assumptions, and translate ideas into actionable process improvements.

Essential Functions

Business Process Management

  • Facilitate process discovery, process mapping, and process improvement workshops with stakeholders across the organization.
  • Document current-state and future-state business processes using BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) standards.
  • Maintain and govern process documentation repositories to ensure consistency, accuracy, and accessibility.
  • Analyze workflows, procedures, and business operations to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop process maps, swim lane diagrams, value stream maps, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist business units in defining process performance measures and key performance indicators (KPIs).
  • Support the development and maintenance of process governance standards, methodologies, and best practices.

Continuous Improvement

  • Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve business performance.
  • Conduct root cause analyses and facilitate problem-solving sessions.
  • Recommend process improvements that reduce waste, improve customer experience, enhance compliance, and increase operational effectiveness.
  • Support implementation and change management activities associated with process improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor and measure the effectiveness of implemented process changes.

Business and Technology Collaboration

  • Collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to understand process and system dependencies.
  • Analyze how applications and technology solutions support business processes and identify alignment opportunities.
  • Participate in software implementation, workflow automation, and digital transformation initiatives as needed.
  • Support user acceptance testing (UAT), process validation, and solution adoption activities.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build collaborative relationships with leaders, subject matter experts, and frontline employees.
  • Facilitate workshops, interviews, and cross-functional working sessions to elicit process knowledge and improvement opportunities.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and process models to stakeholders at various organizational levels.
  • Provide guidance and coaching on process management methodologies and standards (if needed)

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in relevant field
  2. 1-3 years process mapping/analysis
  3. Awareness of flowcharts and swimlane diagrams
  4. Awareness of basic Lean and Six Sigma concepts
  5. Facilitate SME interviews to document process models
  6. Able to harvest requirements in documented process
  7. Process maps, SOPs, workflows
  8. Analyze workflows and KPIs
  9. General business operations

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS: 
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 50 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.
 
WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job.  Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

jobs.title: Wastewater Treatment Operator - All Levels
jobs.description_html:
General Description


Trainee: $20.87 - $26.08 Hourly
Operator I (C License): $23.88 - $31.85 Hourly
Operator II (B License): $25.60 - $34.08 Hourly
Operator III (A License): $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
 
Progression to Operator IV & V will be evaluated based on qualifications and years of experience:
 
Operator IV: $29.26 - $39.02 Hourly 
Operator V: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly 

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain the wastewater treatment plant and the drinking water for the public. This is accomplished by collecting daily meter readings; calibrating lab meters; checking plant equipment; adjusting the SCADA computer; checking charts for trends; performing oil changes and greasing; repairing equipment; collecting daily plant samples; recording dissolved oxygen readings; inspecting chlorine cylinders; communicating problems; creating and fulfilling work orders; completing plant and system checks; verifying equipment operation; evaluating trends; and verifying chemical residuals. Other duties include performing UV maintenance and repair; training employees; troubleshooting for plant malfunctions; creating monthly operation reports; managing monthly water charts and plumage reports; developing a majority of the forms the Water Plants uses; replying to e-mails; performing janitorial work; overseeing fire flow tests; and supervising contractors.

Essential Functions

Trainee:

  1. Performs all operational procedures by checking clarifier blankets; obtaining samples; checking equipment; performing inspections on SCADA communications; cleaning channels or splitter boxes; checking water plants and other facilities; performing preventive maintenance; and administering plant tours.
  2. Communicates with customers and community by sending daily emails; creating reports and facility updates; recording all calibrations of meters or analyzers; inputting data in OPS PAC; developing work orders; directing team meetings; and communicating with bio-solids staff, vendors, and visitors.
  3. Performs all housekeeping duties by hosing down areas with debris; addressing safety concerns; checking for proper drainage; painting; disposing of trash; assisting with landscaping or beautification projects; and ensuring the facility is maintained.
  4. Collects samples for analysis by using gloves and caution in sampling areas; managing sampling containers carefully; avoiding contamination; fulfilling chain of custody forms; and obtaining all information for chain of custody forms.
Operator I (C License):
 1.  Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
 2.   Maintains the plant by completing maintenance work orders; greasing plant equipment; managing rust/corrosion control; and performing housekeeping practices and general cleaning.
 3.  Manages plant repairs by scheduling work orders for internal repair; ensuring all plant equipment in repaired; and assisting mechanics and electricians when necessary.
 4.   All other duties as assigned.

Operator II (B License):
 1.  Performs preventive maintenance by shutting off power; locking out equipment; greasing moving equipment; changing oils in gearboxes; guaranteeing all maintenance activities are safe; and painting equipment.
 2. Controls processes by checking process basins; using odor sensory perception and results from laboratory tests; reviewing the performance of the process; and overseeing the SCADA system.
 3. Performs housekeeping duties by cleaning for spider webs; removing all dirt and debris; maintaining materials and equipment; and ensuring the facility is aesthetically pleasing.
 4. Gives plant tours by evaluating the process and equipment in the treatment process; obtaining daily readings from meters and gauges; maintaining records; and ensuring all equipment functions properly.
 5. Maintains facility logbooks by recording duties and projects; maintaining a record of compliance issues; and maintaining entries of process issues and the integrity of the logbook.
 6. Obtains samples for analysis by using gloves and caution when approaching sampling areas; handling sampling containers carefully; closing sample containers promptly; filling out chain of custody forms; and collecting information for chain of custody form.
 7. All other duties as assigned.

Operator III (A License):
 1.Fulfills water plant daily operations by visiting individual facilities; collecting plant data;  collecting samples to analyze residuals in water leaving the facility; making any necessary adjustments to chemical feed pumps; recording in the logbook all the details; and checking remote wells for normal operations.
  2. Completes monthly work orders by pulling up assigned work orders; reviewing and prioritizing work orders; designating which are to be completed; and completing tasks on a work order.
 3. Remains updated with chemical purchases by approving all chemical purchases for the finance department; copying and filing chemical purchase invoices; submitting purchase orders; and tracking all chemical purchases.
 4. Manages and replies to all company e-mails by opening an e-mail account; filtering through information; saving important data; and replying to emails.
 5. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Trainee:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. This is an entry level position, previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's license.
  4. As a condition of employment, must obtain Class A (CDL) Driver's License within the first six months of employment
Operator I (C License):
 1.   A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
 2.  Minimum of one-year relevant experience.
 3.  Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator C License.
 4.  Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida E Driver's License.

Operator II (B License):
 1.  A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
 2.  Minimum of three years relevant experience.
 3.  Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
 4.  State of Florida Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator B License.
 5.  Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator III (A License):
 1.  A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
 2.  Minimum of three years relevant experience.
 3.  Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
 4.  State of Florida Wastewater Treatment Plant Operator A License.
 5.  Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.

This is accomplished by collecting daily meter readings; calibrating lab meters; checking plant equipment; adjusting the SCADA computer; checking charts for trends; performing oil changes and greasing; repairing equipment; collecting daily plant samples; recording dissolved oxygen readings; inspecting chlorine cylinders; communicating problems; creating and fulfilling work orders; completing plant and system checks; verifying equipment operation; evaluating trends; and verifying chemical residuals. Other duties include performing UV maintenance and repair; training employees; troubleshooting for plant malfunctions; creating monthly operation reports; managing monthly water charts and plumage reports; developing a majority of the forms the Water Plants use; replying to e-mails; performing janitorial work; overseeing fire flow tests; and supervising contractors.

Essential Functions

Trainee:

  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Performs all housekeeping duties by hosing down areas with debris; addressing safety concerns; checking for proper drainage; painting; disposing of trash; assisting with landscaping or beautification projects; and ensuring the facility is maintained.
  3. Collects samples for analysis by using gloves and caution in sampling areas; managing sampling containers carefully; avoiding contaminations; fulfilling chain of custody forms; and obtaining all information for chain of custody forms.
Operator I (C License):
  1. Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
  2. Maintains the plant by completing maintenance work orders; greasing plant equipment; managing rust/corrosion control; and performing housekeeping practices and general cleaning.
  3. Manages plant repairs by scheduling work orders for internal repair; ensuring all plant equipment in repaired; and assisting mechanics and electricians when necessary.
Operator II (B License):
  1. Performs preventive maintenance by shutting off power; locking out equipment; greasing moving equipment; changing oils in gear boxes; guaranteeing all maintenance activities are safe; and painting equipment. 
  2. Controls processes by checking process basins; using odor sensory perception and results from laboratory tests; reviewing the performance of the process; and overseeing the SCADA system. 
  3. Performs housekeeping duties by cleaning for spider webs; removing all dirt and debris; maintaining materials and equipment; and ensuring the facility is aesthetically pleasing. 
  4. Gives plant tours by evaluating the process and equipment in the treatment process; obtaining daily readings from meters and gauges; maintaining records; and ensuring all equipment functions properly. 
  5. Maintains facility log books by recording duties and projects; maintaining a record of compliance issues; and maintaining entries of process issues and the integrity of the log book. 
  6. Obtains samples for analysis by using gloves and caution when approaching sampling areas; handling sampling containers carefully; closing sample containers promptly; filling out chain of custody forms; and collecting information for chain of custody form.
  7. All other duties as assigned.
Operator III (A License):
  1. Fulfills water plant daily operations by visiting individual facilities; collecting plant data; collecting samples to analyze residuals in water leaving the facility; making any necessary adjustments to chemical feed pumps; recording in log book all the details; and checking remote wells for normal operations. 
  2. Completes monthly work orders by pulling up assigned work orders; reviewing and prioritizing work orders; designating which are to being completed; and completing tasks on work order. 
  3. Remains updated with chemical purchases by approving all chemical purchases for the finance department; copying and filing chemical purchase invoices; submitting purchase orders; and tracking all chemical purchases. 
  4. Manages and replies all company e-mails by opening e-mail account; filtering through information; saving important data; and replying to emails.
  5. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

Trainee:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. This is an entry level position, previous relevant work experience is preferred but not required.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator I (C License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of one-year relevant experience.
  3. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator C License.

Operator II (B License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator B License. 
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Operator III (A License):
  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator. 
  2. Minimum of three years relevant experience. 
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. State of Florida Drinking Water Treatment Plant Operator A License.
  5. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.

Physical Demands

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand and walk to a significant degree; use hands to operate tools or feel, and talk or hear. The employee is frequently required to pull, push, kneel, bend, squat, crawl, and twist. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception and ability to adjust focus.

WORKING CONDITIONS:
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Environmental factors include outdoor conditions; rugged terrain, slippery surfaces, varying weather, including, heat, cold, dry, wet weather. In addition, noise, darkness, brightness, vibrations, traffic, biological agents, chemicals, gas/ fumes, magnetic fields, or congested area. Environmental factors include indoor, flat surface, noise, sitting with occasionally walking and standing.
