jobs.title: Cloud Computing Engineer I
jobs.description_html:
Graduate and Research Information Technology (GRIT):

Graduate and Research Information Technology (GRIT) is the dedicated information technology organization supporting UCF’s research enterprise. GRIT delivers specialized technology services, enterprise solutions, and strategic guidance to faculty, staff, and research administration units across the university. Operating within the Office of Research, GRIT encompasses key functional areas such as research administration systems, data and analytics, application development, systems integration, and customer support.

GRIT partners closely with academic and administrative stakeholders through established governance structures and collaborative working groups to ensure that technology initiatives align with UCF’s research priorities. With a commitment to innovation, security, and excellent service delivery, GRIT advances the university’s mission by enabling efficient research operations, supporting compliance and reporting needs, and strengthening technology capabilities that empower discovery and institutional growth.

 

The Opportunity:

The GRIT team within UCF's Office of Research is seeking a Cloud Computing Engineer I to assist in building, deploying, monitoring, and supporting secure, resilient, and cost-effective cloud computing environments that support and enhance research productivity and reliability while following established best practices. This customer-focused position works closely with researchers, systems architects, and other systems team members to support cloud-based research environments and applications.

Responsibilities:

Research Cloud Consultation:

  • Work closely with researchers to help set up research project environments in the cloud, including provisioning and de-provisioning, deploying, managing, operating cloud resources, and supporting research applications hosted in cloud environments.
  • Develop an understanding of research activities through regular engagement with researchers.
  • Assist in estimating cloud costs for research projects.
  • Monitor cloud resources and service health; identify and escalate issues when necessary.
  • May work with research projects with highly restricted data like Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), electronic Protected Health Information (ePHI), personally identifiable information (PII), ITAR-restricted and other protected information as it pertains to various federal agencies and sub-agencies.

Software Development:

  • Support the UCF Research Cloud Environment by developing, deploying, operating, and maintaining cloud services and applications, troubleshooting issues, and helping ensure efficient and reliable cloud-based storage and computing resources.
  • Assist in maintaining Infrastructure as Code templates and deployment automation.
  • Write scripts to automate cloud operations and routine administrative tasks.
  • Perform testing and validation of cloud services and configurations prior to deployment.
  • Apply and maintain security best practices in cloud environments.
  • Follow defined project plans and scopes of work, tracking progress against assigned milestones.

Partnership/Collaboration:

  • Work collaboratively with other team engineers and researchers to build and maintain the applications and services that sit on top of the cloud infrastructure.
  • Assist researchers in gathering and refining technical requirements for cloud-based research projects.
  • Participate in project meetings and technical discussions with researchers and stakeholders to support project objectives.
  • Provide regular communications to project leads with updates.

Documentation/Training:

  • Maintain internal guides and documentation for future contributors.
  • Assist in creating training materials for researchers about the use of cloud environments and related best practices.
  • Support virtual and in-person training events by facilitating logistics, introducing speakers, moderating discussions and participant interactions, providing attendee support, gathering feedback, and assisting with post-event surveys and assessment activities.
  • Develop and apply expertise in specific technologies to support research initiatives and create custom solutions that address researcher needs.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree; or High School Diploma (or equivalent) and 4 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Technical knowledge or hands-on experience — gained through coursework, academic projects, internships, or other applied work — with scripting or programming languages (e.g., Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, or Bash), Linux environments, version control tools (e.g., Git), Infrastructure as Code frameworks (e.g., Terraform), and/or cloud computing platforms (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud).
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences such as researchers and faculty.
  • Demonstrated ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment, collaborating across technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Hands-on experience deploying, configuring, or supporting applications or services in a cloud environment (e.g., AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud) — including through coursework, academic projects, or personal work.
  • Familiarity with cloud security principles and best practices, such as identity and access management (IAM), data encryption, or network security configurations in cloud environments.
  • Experience creating or maintaining technical documentation, process guides, or user-facing instructional materials, as well as hosting workshops for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with or exposure to research, academic, or scientific computing environments — including through academic programs, lab work, or support roles.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $56,030 to $68,636.50. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to maintain residence within driving distance of UCF and be available to report to campus as needed. On-site presence for occasional meetings, special projects, and other business-related activities is an essential function of this role.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you’ll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You’ll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 12 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills, and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

 

Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program 
  • Paid time off, including annual and sick time off and paid holidays
  • Retirement savings options 
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions 
  • Education assistance 
  • And more... For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide.

Dive into our Total Rewards Calculator to discover the diverse selection available to you, giving you a glimpse into the benefits that together shape your comprehensive rewards package at UCF.


Unless explicitly stated on the job posting, it is UCF’s expectation that an employee of UCF will reside in Florida as of the date the employment begins.

 

Additional Requirements related to Research Positions:

Pursuant to Florida State Statute 1010.35, prior to offering employment to certain individuals in research-related positions, UCF is required to conduct additional screening. Applicants subject to additional screening include any citizen of a foreign country who is not a permanent resident of the U.S., or who is a citizen or permanent resident but is affiliated with or has had at least 1 year of education, employment, or training in China, Cuba, Iran, Russia, North Korea, Syria, or Venezuela.

The additional screening requirements only apply to research-related positions, including, but not limited to faculty, graduate positions, individuals compensated by research grants or contract funds, postdoctoral positions, undergraduate positions, visiting assistant professors, and visiting research associates.

jobs.title: Administrative Coordinator II
jobs.description_html:
UCF Global:

UCF Global at the University of Central Florida functions as the primary international hub for students, faculty, and staff. Through strong partnerships, UCF Global is committed to increasing international and local mobility and enhancing the university’s global competency. Encompassing the English language programs and multiple support services for the international population on campus, UCF Global aides in transforming the lives of the UCF and global community.

 

The Opportunity: 

This position reports to the Director of UCF Abroad and serves as lead support for administrative and office functions of the unit.

The Administrative Coordinator II assists unit leadership with: financial processes and budget management; prep for student recruitment marketing and events; occasionally assist with data collection and reporting; and primary contact for daily office operations.

 

Responsibilities:

  • In collaboration with the Study Abroad Coordinators, liaise with study abroad faculty leaders and assist with budget creation, travel advance requests and advance reconciliation, and reconcile faculty-led program budgets.
  • Manage day-to-day office operations for UCF Abroad, including planning and scheduling meetings, unit events, and hosting visitors. Serve as property custodian for department and manages requests for ID card building access. Facilitate resolution of IT issues and requests for user access for unit.
  • Coordinate with department leadership on student fee and credit posting process for all study abroad activities.
  • Make departmental purchases and reconcile department purchasing card transactions.
  • Process travel requests and reimbursements for unit staff.
  • Assist the Director and the unit with HR and personnel issues. Support the unit with searches, hiring, and on-boarding processes to ensure compliance with university policies.
  • Work closely with the Director, UCF Abroad, the Office of the Associate Vice President, UCF Global, and the Academic Affairs Business Center (AABC) to ensure accurate budget, payroll, procurement, and HR functions and policies are followed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 2+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Computer skills in MS Office Suite including but not limited to Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Outlook.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills.
  • International travel and/or study abroad experience.
  • Experience in higher education.
  • Experience with budget management and HR processes.
  • Accounting experience is desirable.
  • Experience with Workday and PeopleSoft.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated hourly range for this position is $20.29 - $21.46 ($42,367- $44,805 annually). The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • Prefer candidate with the ability to communicate in both English and an additional language in order to work effectively with customers and team members.
  • Occasional local, out of state, and overnight travel required to support student recruitment efforts.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

jobs.title: Controls Specialist II
jobs.description_html:
University Operations:

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

Join our team as a Controls Specialist II where you will play a pivotal role in providing technical support, retro commissioning and first-analysis of HVAC performance investigations for coordinated operations and maintenance of HVAC systems to provide a safe, functional, clean, efficient and attractive learning environment. At this level, the employee is expected to have intermediate skills in HVAC and Controls Systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform preventative maintenance on HVAC building automation systems and related equipment in order to ensure continuous operation and prevent equipment interruptions through proactive analysis of the BAS front end and back end software platforms.
  • Install, repair, replace and recalibrate BAS controllers, terminal devices and ancillary components to maintain continuously commissioned HVAC BAS controls. 
  • Perform continuous updates and improvements to system front end graphics, back end programming and parametric configurations, databases and networks. 
  • Work in conjunction with the Utility and Energy Services commissioning /retro commissioning team to deliver BAS operational and energy efficiency improvements.

jobs.title: Travel & Procurement Specialist III
jobs.description_html:
Knights Experience Team (kNEXT):

The University of Central Florida’s (UCF’s) the Knights Experience Team (kNEXT) primarily provides customer service to the Finance Business Centers (FBCs) and the Human Resources Business Centers (HRBC's) employees, assisting with various tasks as needed. kNEXT also provides administrative support services to staff across all colleges and divisions of the University. kNEXT is designed to reduce the administrative burden on individual colleges, consolidate transaction-based functions, create economies of scale, and improve backroom process efficiency so the colleges can better focus resources on their mission.

The team is made up of HR Specialists and Travel/Procurement Specialists, who will provide information and support across campus, reduce administrative burden, and empower employees to learn and grow. These Specialists will operate as campus experts on processes and procedures, support training and development, provide specialized reporting and analytics, and support central office transactions. All employees within kNEXT will also work to continuously improve processes and workflows.

The purpose of kNEXT is to ensure that the services provided meet or exceed expected performance levels and satisfy the needs of the faculty/staff/students (colleges/divisions).

 

The Opportunity: 

The Knights Experience Team (kNEXT) is seeking a Travel & Procurement Specialist III to lead a team of specialists supporting travel and procurement for one of the nation's largest universities. With more than 70,000 students and 13,000 employees, UCF relies on purchasing and travel processes that are accurate, efficient, and built to serve colleges and divisions across campus. As a working lead, you'll guide and develop your team, serve as a go-to expert for campus partners, and help shape the processes that keep the university moving. Bring your leadership to UCF and help build a team that empowers thousands of faculty and staff to focus on what matters most.

 

Responsibilities:

Team Leadership

  • Supervisory responsibilities, including hiring and training, monitoring performance and providing feedback, maintaining leave requests and personnel records, setting goals and objectives and monitoring accomplishments, enforcing customer service standards, and resolving complex issues.

Procurement, Contracts, and Payments

  • Support requests for the procurement of goods and services ensuring applicable policies and regulations are adhered to and transactions are processed timely and properly reflect the receipt of goods or services.
  • Research suppliers and obtain quotes for goods and services, as needed.
  • Assist with the development of solicitations for bids and participate in the development of contracts and agreements.
  • Identify and review applicable contracts or the need for a Waiver of Competition and Sole Source Certification in accordance with policies and regulations.
  • Initiate and review requisitions, manage purchase orders, and initiate change orders, as needed.
  • Create receipts and supplier invoices or purchasing card transactions to ensure timely payments.
  • Reconcile/verify purchasing card transactions ensuring applicable policies and regulations are adhered to and transactions are allowable, required documentation is provided, and transactions are accurate.

Travel

  • Support travel requests creating and reviewing Spend Authorizations and Expense Reports.
  • Assist with travel arrangements, receipt/documentation collection, and travel advance and reimbursement requests to ensuring applicable policies and regulations are adhered to.

Expertise, Training, and Process Improvement

  • Support Travel/Procurement Coordinators within the Finance Business Centers (FBCs) as experts on procurement-related and travel-related processes and procedures.
  • Support travel and procurement training efforts.
  • Continuously review and improve processes to increase operational efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Other job-related duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications: 

High School Diploma or equivalent and (4+) years of relevant experience or combination of relevant comparable education and experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience supervising staff in a working lead capacity, including hiring, training, setting expectations, providing performance feedback, and addressing performance concerns.
  • 3+ years of experience in purchasing, travel, accounts payable/receivable, or related financial operations.
  • Working knowledge of financial, purchasing, and travel rules, regulations, policies, and procedures, including purchasing card, spend authorization, and expense report processes.
  • Proven ability to set and uphold customer service standards for a team while delivering high-quality service to internal and campus partners.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to coach others, navigate difficult conversations, and positively influence colleagues and stakeholders.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the sound judgment to resolve complex issues and escalate appropriately.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a high-volume environment.
  • Experience with Workday, PeopleSoft, or a similar ERP system, and proficiency in Microsoft Outlook, Excel, and Teams.
  • Bachelor’s degree.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary for this role is $54,203. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional vacancies in this department.

Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?  

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you’ll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You’ll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 12 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills, and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

 

Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program 
  • Paid time off, including annual and sick time off and paid holidays
  • Retirement savings options 
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions 
  • Education assistance 
  • And more…For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide.

 

Dive into our Total Rewards Calculator to discover the diverse selection available to you, giving you a glimpse into the benefits that together shape your comprehensive rewards package at UCF.

jobs.description_html:
Advancement & Partnerships:

Join our dynamic and growing Advancement & Partnerships team as we work together to power partnerships and transform lives through philanthropy.

Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world.  Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.

 

The Opportunity:

The Advancement & Partnerships division leads the university’s fundraising and alumni engagement work. We’re looking for a Prospect Research Analyst II to help our fundraisers find and understand the alumni, individuals, companies, and foundations most likely to support UCF.

Working with the Assistant Director of Prospect Research and the broader research team, you’ll turn public information into clear, confidential profiles that shape how we build donor relationships. Your research will inform everything from annual giving to the university’s largest gifts, and your work will help prepare UCF’s president and senior leaders for conversations with key guests at university events.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Research and analyze biographical, business, and financial information on alumni, individuals, corporations, and foundations, then distill findings into concise, confidential profiles that support fundraisers at every gift level.
  • Assign and refine estimated giving capacity ratings using wealth screening data and help develop rating methods based on industry’s best practices.
  • Monitor news, job announcements, and other sources to spot new prospects and relevant updates, alerting fundraising staff when follow-up is needed.
  • Keep donor and alumni records accurate by entering new information and verifying and cleaning existing records.
  • Lead the event briefing process with our donor experience team and campus partners, preparing the university president and senior leadership with background on select guests.
  • Respond to high-priority and ad hoc research requests, working with the team to plan and manage how requests are fulfilled.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in prospect research or donor research in higher education or a nonprofit setting.
  • Working knowledge of fundraising processes and how research supports gift strategy at different levels.
  • Experience with wealth screening tools and assigning capacity ratings.
  • Ability to interpret financial and business information, such as public company filings, real estate records, and foundation tax returns.
  • Experience maintaining records in a donor or constituent database.
  • Strong writing skills, with the ability to summarize complex information briefly and clearly.
  • Experience preparing briefing materials for senior executives.
  • Sound judgment in handling confidential information, with an understanding of ethical standards for prospect research.
  • Ability to manage multiple high-priority requests on tight timelines.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary for a well-qualified candidate is between $44,056.80 and $51,000.
  • Advancement and Partnerships values the unique contributions that each team member brings to our division. The final determination of a successful candidate's starting salary will vary based on several factors, including education and relevant experience. The anticipated pay scale indicated for this position generally applies to candidates who meet the minimum requirements and several of the preferred qualifications outlined above. All offers are contingent on successful background and reference screens.

Advancement & Partnerships: 
 Join our dynamic and growing Advancement & Partnerships team as we work together to power partnerships and transform lives through philanthropy.
 Together, we can unleash the potential of people and ideas to positively change the world. Your efforts on our team will help us to build the University for the Future.
 The Opportunity :
 The Advancement & Partnerships division leads the university’s fundraising and alumni engagement work. We’re looking for a Prospect Research Analyst II to help our fundraisers find and understand the alumni, individuals, companies, and foundations most likely to support UCF.
 Working with the Assistant Director of Prospect Research and the broader research team, you’ll turn public information into clear, confidential profiles that shape how we build donor relationships. Your research will inform everything from annual giving to the university’s largest gifts, and your work will help prepare UCF’s president and senior leaders for conversations with key guests at university events.
 Responsibilities: 
 Research and analyze biographical, business, and financial information on alumni, individuals, corporations, and foundations, then distill findings into concise, confidential profiles that support fundraisers at every gift level.
 Assign and refine estimated giving capacity ratings using wealth screening data and help develop rating methods based on industry’s best practices.
 Monitor news, job announcements, and other sources to spot new prospects and relevant updates, alerting fundraising staff when follow-up is needed.
 Keep donor and alumni records accurate by entering new information and verifying and cleaning existing records.
 Lead the event briefing process with our donor experience team and campus partners, preparing the university president and senior leadership with background on select guests.
 Respond to high-priority and ad hoc research requests, working with the team to plan and manage how requests are fulfilled.
 Minimum Qualifications : 
 Bachelor's degree and 2+ years of related experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6) .
 Preferred Qualifications :
 Experience in prospect research or donor research in higher education or a nonprofit setting.
 Working knowledge of fundraising processes and how research supports gift strategy at different levels.
 Experience with wealth screening tools and assigning capacity ratings.
 Ability to interpret financial and business information, such as public company filings, real estate records, and foundation tax returns.
 Experience maintaining records in a donor or constituent database.
 Strong writing skills, with the ability to summarize complex information briefly and clearly.
 Experience preparing briefing materials for senior executives.
 Sound judgment in handling confidential information, with an understanding of ethical standards for prospect research.
 Ability to manage multiple high-priority requests on tight timelines.

jobs.title: Compliance & Performance Reporting Analyst (TEMP)
jobs.description_html:
Pegasus Research Institute:

Pegasus Research Institute (PRI) is the University of Central Florida’s applied research institute, bringing together expertise from across UCF to solve complex, real-world challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

This position is responsible for monitoring adherence to institutional requirements, sponsor agreements, policies, and procedures while ensuring the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of programmatic, operational, and financial reporting. The analyst conducts reviews, maintains compliance documentation, tracks corrective actions, and develops reporting tools that support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.


Responsibilities:

  • Monitor compliance with institutional policies, sponsor requirements, agreements, and established procedures.
  • Maintain documentation, records, and evidence necessary to support audits, reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Perform evidence-quality testing and document-control activities to ensure reporting accuracy and audit readiness.
  • Develop and maintain reporting calendars, key performance indicators (KPIs), compliance checklists, and control schedules.
  • Track risks, exceptions, corrective actions, and compliance issues, ensuring appropriate follow-up and resolution.
  • Conduct analytical reviews and reconciliations across programmatic, project, operational, and financial reports.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc reports that communicate performance, compliance status, trends, and risks to leadership.
  • Identify reporting discrepancies, process gaps, and control weaknesses and recommend corrective actions.
  • Support internal and external audits by gathering documentation, coordinating responses, and tracking remediation efforts.
  • Assist with policy interpretation and provide guidance on compliance-related processes and requirements.
  • Collaborate with program, project, finance, and operational teams to improve reporting quality and process efficiency.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen compliance controls and operational effectiveness.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with 5-8 years in compliance, audit, sponsored research, quality assurance, internal controls, or performance reporting.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Agreement, procedure, and institutional-requirement alignment.
  • Evidence-quality testing, audit readiness, and document control.
  • Reporting calendars, KPI definitions, control schedules, and review checklists.
  • Risk, corrective-action, exception, and issue tracking.
  • Analytical review and reconciliation across program, project, and financial reporting.
  • Policy interpretation and process improvement in regulated environments.

Additional Application Materials Required:

  • In addition to the online application, candidates should upload a cover letter and current curriculum vitae.
  • UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website.
  • The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to Abram Walton, Abram.Walton@ucf.edu and Wayne Fogel, Wayne.Fogel@ucf.edu


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

The anticipated hourly range for this position is $37.35 - $59.87. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

This position is responsible for translating complex research, technical, and operational information into clear, accurate, and audience-appropriate communications for sponsors, leadership, researchers, partners, and the public. The incumbent coordinates review processes, ensures compliance with institutional standards, and maintains the quality and consistency of publications across multiple communication channels.


Responsibilities:

  • Translate complex research, scientific, technical, and programmatic information into clear and accessible content for diverse audiences.
  • Produce and maintain reports, newsletters, presentations, fact sheets, website content, executive summaries, publications, and communication materials.
  • Support the development of communication products that highlight research outcomes, program accomplishments, and institutional initiatives.
  • Coordinate content collection, drafting, editing, and publication schedules for recurring communications and reporting activities.
  • Develop workshop, conference, meeting, and event materials, including agendas, presentations, participant communications, summaries, and follow-up content.
  • Conduct editorial review and quality assurance to ensure accuracy, consistency, clarity, and adherence to established standards.
  • Ensure compliance with accessibility requirements, institutional branding standards, attribution requirements, and publication guidelines.
  • Manage document version control, publication records, and content approval workflows.
  • Coordinate technical, legal, compliance, sponsor, and institutional reviews to ensure timely publication and distribution of materials.
  • Verify factual accuracy and consistency across publications, reports, and communication products.

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with 3-6 years in content development, digital communications, technical editing, events, public information, or research translation.

  • Technical and executive writing, editing, and quality assurance.
  • Research translation and plain-language communication for varied audiences.
  • Presentation, publication, newsletter, report, and website-content development.
  • Workshop and event materials, logistics, summaries, and follow-up content.
  • Accessibility, brand, attribution, factual-accuracy, and version-control standards.

Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

The position provides strategic and operational leadership for large-scale research programs and initiatives within the institute. This position is responsible for planning, coordinating, and overseeing complex sponsored research activities, ensuring successful execution of program objectives, contractual requirements, budgets, schedules, and deliverables. The incumbent serves as a key liaison among principal investigators, research staff, institutional leadership, sponsors, and external partners, supporting the institute's research mission through effective program management, stakeholder engagement, and continuous process improvement.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead the planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout of complex research programs and projects.
  • Develop and maintain integrated program plans, work breakdown structures, schedules, budgets, milestones, and performance metrics.
  • Coordinate and lead cross-functional and multi-institutional teams to ensure alignment of program goals, deliverables, and timelines.
  • Monitor program performance and progress, proactively identifying and mitigating risks, issues, dependencies, and changes that may impact project outcomes.
  • Ensure timely and accurate sponsor reporting and facilitate deliverable reviews and acceptance processes.
  • Prepare executive-level briefings, program updates, and strategic reports for institute leadership and external stakeholders.
  • Support proposal development, project startup activities, and ongoing program administration for sponsored research awards.
  • Facilitate communication and collaboration among researchers, sponsors, partners, and administrative units.
  • Oversee program budgets and resource allocations to ensure effective stewardship of sponsored funds.
  • Promote consistent project and program management practices across the institute, including the development of tools, templates, and standard operating procedures.

Minimum Qualifications:

Master's degree from an accredited institution with 8-12 years of experience leading large, multidisciplinary research, engineering, or technology programs.

  • Integrated program plans, work breakdown structures, schedules, budgets, and milestones.
  • Sponsor reporting, deliverable acceptance, and executive briefings.
  • Leadership of cross-functional and multi-institution teams.
  • Risk, issue, dependency, and change management.
  • Mentoring program managers and promoting consistent execution practices.
  • Working knowledge of federal, state, industry, and sponsored-research award structures.

jobs.title: Senior Compensation Partner
jobs.description_html:
Human Resources:

UCF Human Resources is a trusted partner and catalyst in making UCF the best place to work and positively impact our community by working together to unleash the potential of everyone at UCF. We make it our mission to support and advance UCF’s goals by fostering a positive and engaging work environment while identifying and responding to the changing needs of our community.


The Opportunity:

UCF Human Resources is seeking a Senior Compensation Partner to serve as the lead compensation consultant for one of the nation's largest universities. With more than 70,000 students and 13,000 employees, UCF makes pay decisions that shape how we attract, retain, and reward the people behind our mission. As a subject matter expert and technical leader, you'll turn compensation priorities into the programs and practices that support employees across the university. You'll also lead the systems and reporting efforts that power those decisions, and you'll mentor and guide colleagues across the compensation team. Bring your expertise to UCF and help build the future of how we recognize and reward our people.


Responsibilities:

Compensation Expertise and Technical Leadership

  • Serve as the lead compensation consultant and subject matter expert, independently resolving complex issues across base pay, salary structures, job architecture, position classification, job evaluations, market pricing, and internal equity.
  • Partner with HR business partners and institutional leaders to develop practical, data-informed compensation solutions that maintain equity, policy compliance, and governance.
  • Provide day-to-day technical guidance and mentorship to compensation colleagues as a primary resource for complex inquiries.

Workday HCM and Advanced Compensation

  • Lead optimization and continuous improvement of Workday HCM and serve as the functional owner of Workday Advanced Compensation, including annual salary program execution.
  • Partner with the Enterprise ERP team to define requirements, perform functional and unit testing, and support implementation through process redesign, documentation, and end-user training.

Projects and Continuous Improvement

  • Lead and support compensation projects, programs, and process improvements, translating leadership priorities into actionable plans, tools, and deliverables.

Compensation Strategy and Salary Programs

  • Support the Senior Director of Compensation in university-wide compensation strategy, planning, and administration of salary programs, including annual salary programs and merit increases.

Reporting, Analytics, and Data Governance

  • Provide functional leadership for compensation reporting, analytics, and dashboards, including Power BI, in collaboration with Enterprise Reporting and HR technology partners.
  • Support compensation data audits, validation procedures, and standardized reporting practices that strengthen data integrity.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of progressive compensation experience, including market pricing, job evaluations, and position classification.
  • Experience serving as a consultant and trusted advisor to HR business partners and organizational leaders, providing sound judgment and data-informed compensation recommendations.
  • Experience mentoring, training, or serving as a technical resource for compensation colleagues.
  • Experience with Workday or a similar Human Resources Information System (HRIS) to support compensation administration and ensure data accuracy and integrity.
  • Experience leading or contributing to compensation or HR systems projects and process improvements, including requirements gathering, testing, process redesign, and end-user training.
  • Experience supporting the administration of enterprise-wide salary programs, such as annual salary programs and merit increases.
  • Experience developing compensation reports, dashboards, or analytics, such as Power BI, and supporting data audits or validation to strengthen data integrity.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary for this position is $110,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Classification Title: Compensation Partner III

Are you ready to unleash YOUR potential?

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you’ll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You’ll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 12 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills, and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.


Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program
  • Paid time off, including annual and sick time off and paid holidays
  • Retirement savings options
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions
  • Education assistance
  • And more…For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide.

Dive into our Total Rewards Calculator to discover the diverse selection available to you, giving you a glimpse into the benefits that together shape your comprehensive rewards package at UCF.

Unless explicitly stated on the job posting, it is UCF’s expectation that an employee of UCF will reside in Florida as of the date the employment begins.

jobs.description_html:
Rosen College of Hospitality Management:

The Rosen College of Hospitality Management is comprised of approximately 100 wide-ranging faculty and staff members that represent over 18 different countries and are recognized for their research, teaching skills, and industry impact. Rosen College students are exposed to some of the most modern and well-designed learning laboratories as they pursue one of the many B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. majors offered.


Learn more about UCF’s Rosen College of Hospitality Management.


The Opportunity:

The UCF Rosen College of Hospitality Management is one of the most renowned hospitality programs in the world, and the students who move through its culinary labs are the next generation of industry leaders. As a Food and Beverage Specialist II, you'll be right in the middle of that experience — working alongside the college's Chefs to support hands-on undergraduate culinary lab sessions, maintain the quality and safety of the culinary and beverage lab environments, and help bring large-scale catered events to life.


We are currently seeking a Food and Beverage Specialist II, who brings real kitchen experience and takes pride in both craft and consistency to join this dynamic team. You'll play a meaningful role in shaping the day-to-day learning environment for students while contributing to the operational excellence that Rosen College is known for. If you're passionate about food service and ready to bring your expertise into an academic setting where it truly makes an impact — this is your opportunity.
 

Responsibilities:

  • Assist the Chefs and/or Food & Beverage Specialist III, in training UCF undergraduate students during lab sessions and maintain organization and cleanliness in the culinary and beverage labs.
  • Assist the Food & Beverage Specialist III in planning and executing advanced and complex catered events, internal or external, on the Rosen Campus.
  • Sustain the cleanliness, organization, and safety of all food and beverage supplies, equipment, and facilities on the Rosen College Campus.
  • Adhere to and ensure proper receiving, storage, and inventory (FIFO) practices, and assist with the pickup and delivery of food and beverage products and supplies.
  • Additional duties as assigned based on the needs of the department, college, and UCF as directed by the department head, chair, and dean.

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience working in a fast-paced culinary, restaurant, or fast-food environment.
  • Experience assisting with training, mentoring, or guiding others in a food service or kitchen environment.
  • Basic knowledge of food safety, sanitation, and safe food handling practices.
  • Experience supporting catered events, banquets, or large-volume food preparation.
  • Previous experience working in a higher education food lab or similar setting is highly desirable.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Adaptability and willingness to learn new techniques and processes.
  • Effective collaboration within a team, with the ability to work independently when required.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with a customer service–focused approach.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


The anticipated hourly range for this position is $15.66 to $17.23 per hour. The final rate will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


Additional evening or weekend hours may be required to support business needs, events, or project deadlines.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

jobs.title: Visiting Instructor or Lecturer, School of Teacher Education
jobs.description_html:
The Opportunity  

The School of Teacher Education (STE) in the College of Community Innovation and Education (CCIE) is dedicated to preparing and retaining exceptional student education teachers and professional educators who serve children and adults with special needs. In collaboration with Central Florida partners and CCIE's Toni Jennings Exceptional Education Institute (TJEEI), STE provides families of children with disabilities, UCF faculty and students, and educators with access to current information, resources and learning opportunities. Through teaching and research clinics, UCF faculty and students work to offer students with disabilities and their families services focused on assessment, behavior, reading, mathematics and community counseling. 


The School of Teacher Education is seeking applications for a 9-month, non-tenure earning, visiting instructor or lecturer. The successful candidate will teach four courses in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) program each semester, is expected to lead the ABA and BCBA programs, and provide administrative support for the current ABA accreditation, ABA attestations, and potentially support grant administration. The incumbent will also work with graduate affairs on behalf of STE with course substitutions.


This position is located on the Orlando campus and is anticipated to begin Spring 2027.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Instructor: A master’s degree in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution; Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials; and a minimum of five years of directly relevant professional experience in applied behavior analysis or a closely related area. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.
  • Lecturer: A terminal degree (e.g., PhD, EdD) in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution, and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctoral-level Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA-D) credentials
  • PK-20 teaching experience
  • Experience with grant-related work (e.g., administration/writing, implementation, support)

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A curriculum vitae. 
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest. 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials. 

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Dan Ezell at Dan.Ezell@ucf.edu, Search Committee Chair.  

Special Instructions to the Applicants: 

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 


This is a visiting, 9-month, non-tenure track appointment with benefits, annually renewable for up to four academic years (maximum).

Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted without an end date may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

As a next-generation public research university and Forbes-ranked top employer in Florida, we are a community of thinkers, doers, creators, innovators, healers, and leaders striving to create broader prosperity and help shape a better future. No matter what your role is, when you join Knight Nation, you’ll play an integral role at one of the most impactful universities in the country. You’ll be met with opportunities to connect and collaborate with talented faculty, staff, and students across 13 colleges and multiple campuses, engaging in impactful work that makes a positive difference. Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.


Working at UCF has its perks! UCF offers:

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program.  
  • Paid time off, including annual (12-month faculty) and sick time off and paid holidays. 
  • Retirement savings options.  
  • Employee discounts, including tickets to many Orlando attractions.  
  • Education assistance. 
  • Flexible work environment.  
  • And more…For more benefits information, view the UCF Employee Benefits Guide click here.

Unless explicitly stated on the job posting, it is UCF’s expectation that an employee of UCF will reside in Florida as of the date the employment begins.


Additional Requirements related to Research Positions:

Pursuant to Florida State Statute 1010.35, prior to offering employment to certain individuals in research-related positions, UCF is required to conduct additional screening. Applicants subject to additional screening include any citizen of a foreign country who is not a permanent resident of the U.S., or who is a citizen or permanent resident but is affiliated with or has had at least 1 year of education, employment, or training in China, Cuba, Iran, Russia, North Korea, Syria, or Venezuela.


The additional screening requirements only apply to research-related positions, including, but not limited to faculty, graduate positions, individuals compensated by research grants or contract funds, post-doctoral positions, undergraduate positions, visiting assistant professors, and visiting research associates.

jobs.title: Senior Licensing Associate
jobs.description_html:
The Opportunity:

As part of UCF's Technology Transfer Office, the Senior Licensing Associate position manages the transfer of physical science technologies from university into commercial sectors. Manages technology review, intellectual property (IP) legal protection, IP license negotiations, and IP promotion in media and at scientific and technology related events.


Responsibilities:

  • Manages the protection and licensing of a portion of the UCF Research Foundation IP portfolio which includes patents, trademarks and copyrights in the areas of physical sciences. Drafts and negotiates license agreements and other types of agreements, including material transfer, inter-institutional, and nondisclosure agreements.
  • Assesses and evaluates new technologies disclosed to Technology Transfer. Identifies commercial uses and recommends appropriate legal protection and ensures adherence to IP laws and regulations.
  • Reviews and edits promotional materials to advertise new technologies to prospective industry partners. Leads outreach to commercialize technologies and promotes new technologies at scientific conferences and to business communities.
  • Reviews, edits, and negotiates IP terms and conditions for UCF sponsored research activities. Coordinates IP matters between contract manager, general counsel, principal investigator, and external sponsor/external counsel.
  • Attracts and cultivates relationships with university researchers, entrepreneurs and industry partners to drive licensing deal flow and potential sponsored research activity.
  • Supervises, trains, and instructs one or more intellectual property specialist, licensing assistant, students and/or interns.
  • Conducts workshops and delivers presentations to educate internal and external communities on Technology Transfer matters, best practices and IP policies.
  • Attends professional trade conferences.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Engineering (e.g., Mechanical, Civil, Electrical) or a related physical science field.
  • 3+ years of demonstrated success in drafting, negotiating, and implementing legal agreements.
  • Strong customer service orientation with experience collaborating with faculty, legal teams, and external partners.
  • Proven business development and finance acumen.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build and maintain strong relationships.
  • Ability to evaluate market potential and effectively communicate with different stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with patent assessment and market research methodologies.
  • Prior experience in technology transfer and outbound software licensing.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $80,000 - $95,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity here at UCF, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 
  •  Classification Title: License & Patent Associate II

Your time at UCF will provide you with many meaningful opportunities to grow, you’ll work alongside talented colleagues on complex projects that will challenge you and help you gain new skills, and you’ll have countless rewarding experiences that go well beyond a paycheck.

  • Benefit packages, including Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Spending, and Employee Assistance Program   
  • Paid time off, including annual and sick time off and paid holidays

jobs.title: Manager, Accounting
jobs.description_html:
Financial Affairs:

Financial Affairs partners with our UCF community to continuously improve and deliver outstanding administrative and financial services through innovative business and technological solutions and sound fiscal stewardship.


The Opportunity:

The University of Central Florida's Financial Affairs division is seeking a dynamic and experienced Accounting Manager to lead and oversee its student financial cashiering services, in-person and email customer service units, and management of all campus cash/check collections. In this high-impact role, you will be responsible for directing, developing, and guiding a team while ensuring the successful completion of all tasks, projects, and administrative mandates that advance the department's and university's financial goals. If you are a detail-oriented accounting professional with a passion for operational excellence, compliance, and leadership in a fast-paced university environment, we invite you to bring your expertise to Knight Nation.


Responsibilities:

  • Directs and manages the university's main depository account operations, including high-volume deposits exceeding $600 million annually; provides guidance to personnel on administrative policies and procedures to effectively manage administrative and fiscal operations.
  • Hires, trains, coaches, and evaluates staff direct reports.
  • Directs and manages the preparation of daily, monthly, and annual financial reports and reconciliations across two financial systems — Oracle PeopleSoft and Workday; evaluates and modifies business processes to adapt to these systems.
  • Manages the opening, closing, and operations of university cashiering offices; manages cash, check, and wire deposits and reviews and monitors outstanding deposits to the general ledger; interprets, formulates, and implements operational and UCF policies and procedures.
  • Recommends, creates, and implements long- and short-term strategic plan goals and operational plans; analyzes financial functions and makes recommendations for department controls.
  • Responds to audit reports and ensures the continuous existence of internal controls to safeguard and protect the university's funds and other assets; serves as liaison among functional areas and departments.
  • Interprets and ensures compliance with Florida Statutes, BOG regulations, and UCF policies and regulations; responsible for obtaining and maintaining the required annual certification for Student Account Services with respect to Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Experience in accounting or financial operations within a higher education or public sector environment.
  • Demonstrated experience managing financial reporting and reconciliations in enterprise financial systems, such as Oracle PeopleSoft or Workday.
  • Experience managing and developing a team of professional staff.
  • Familiarity with Florida Statutes, Board of Governors regulations, and public university financial policies and procedures.
  • Proven ability to develop and implement internal controls, audit responses, and process improvement initiatives.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate across functional areas.
  • Knowledge of Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance standards and experience maintaining related certifications.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $75,000 to $80,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

 Manages the opening, closing, and operations of university cashiering offices; manages cash, check, and wire deposits and reviews and monitors outstanding deposits to the general ledger; interprets, formulates, and implements operational and UCF policies and procedures.
 Recommends, creates, and implements long- and short-term strategic plan goals and operational plans; analyzes financial functions and makes recommendations for department controls.
 Responds to audit reports and ensures the continuous existence of internal controls to safeguard and protect the university's funds and other assets; serves as liaison among functional areas and departments.
 Interprets and ensures compliance with Florida Statutes, BOG regulations, and UCF policies and regulations; responsible for obtaining and maintaining the required annual certification for Student Account Services with respect to Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance.
 Other duties as assigned.
 Minimum Qualifications: 
 Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6) .

 Advanced degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or a related field.
 Experience in accounting or financial operations within a higher education or public sector environment.
 Demonstrated experience managing financial reporting and reconciliations in enterprise financial systems, such as Oracle PeopleSoft or Workday.
 Experience managing and developing a team of professional staff.
 Familiarity with Florida Statutes, Board of Governors regulations, and public university financial policies and procedures.
 Proven ability to develop and implement internal controls, audit responses, and process improvement initiatives.
 Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills with the ability to effectively collaborate across functional areas.
 Knowledge of Payment Card Industry (PCI) compliance standards and experience maintaining related certifications.

jobs.description_html:
University Operations: 

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience. 

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.


The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking to hire Project Portfolio Managers. This role is responsible for providing leadership, oversight, and strategic direction for a portfolio of capital construction, deferred maintenance, and renewal projects with a total value exceeding $140 million. This position leads a team of project management professionals, manages client relationships, and ensures projects are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in accordance with university standards and objectives. Serving as the primary point of contact for assigned clients, the Project Portfolio Manager oversees projects throughout the full lifecycle, from planning and design through construction and closeout. This position reports to the Senior Director and/or Assistant Vice President of Planning, Design & Construction.


Responsibilities:

Portfolio Leadership & Team Management

  • Lead and oversee a portfolio of capital construction, renovation, deferred maintenance, and renewal projects.
  • Manage project workload assignments and forecast future resource needs to support portfolio objectives.
  • Provide leadership, mentorship, and performance management for project management staff, including Senior Project Managers.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for portfolio clients and maintain strong stakeholder relationships.
  • Monitor portfolio budgets, schedules, progress, quality, and performance metrics to proactively identify and resolve issues.
  • Ensure compliance with established policies, procedures, standards, and project management practices.

Project Management & Delivery

  • Direct and coordinate all phases of complex construction projects from planning and design through construction and closeout.
  • Manage contractors, architects, engineers, and consultants to ensure successful project execution.
  • Review project scope, plans, specifications, and construction documents to ensure constructability and minimize change orders.
  • Monitor project budgets, schedules, and quality standards to support successful outcomes.
  • Provide technical guidance regarding design and construction challenges and facilitate timely resolution of issues.
  • Conduct site visits and inspections to verify compliance with contract requirements, building codes, safety regulations, and university standards.
  • Support campus sustainability initiatives through new construction and renovation projects.

Contract Administration & Continuous Improvement

  • Assist in the preparation of Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Invitations to Bid (ITBs), and other procurement documents.
  • Provide guidance in the selection of architectural, engineering, and construction service providers.
  • Support reporting and performance tracking for project portfolios and team productivity.
  • Promote continuous improvement through process enhancements, lessons learned, and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience managing large-scale capital construction portfolios.
  • Experience supervising and mentoring project management professionals.
  • Knowledge of public-sector or higher education construction practices.
  • Experience working with architects, engineers, contractors, and consulting firms.
  • Strong leadership, stakeholder engagement, and strategic planning skills.
  • Professional certification such as PMP, CCM, or related credential.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $89,076 - $117,747. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional Construction Project Portfolio Manager vacancies in this department.

jobs.title: Arborist III
jobs.description_html:
Facilities and Business Operations:

Facilities and Business Operations at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.


Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.


The Opportunity:

The Landscape and Natural Resources Department at Facilities and Business Operations is seeking an experienced Arborist III to lead the Tree Care team. This is a hands-on leadership opportunity ideal for an arborist who is passionate about tree care and wants to continue working in the field while taking on greater responsibility. The selected candidate will work alongside crew members, providing technical expertise and leading daily tree care operations that support the health, functionality, and aesthetics of UCF's tree canopy.


As the lead Arborist, you will coordinate and participate in a wide range of arboricultural activities, including tree installation, pruning, removals, root remediation, and disease management, while ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards. You will also serve as a secondary point of contact for customers, representing the department through effective communication, problem-solving, and a commitment to exceptional service. Responsibilities may evolve based on organizational needs.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead and supervise the daily operations of the tree crew, ensuring tasks are performed safely, efficiently, and to the highest standards.
  • Tree installation, pruning, removals, stump grinding, root remediation, and disease management.
  • Manage workflow, training, and employee development to maintain optimal performance.
  • Maintain and oversee all tree care equipment, including chipper trucks, brush chippers, chainsaws, pole saws, aerial platforms, stump grinders, root pruners, air spades, and compressors.
  • Ensure tools and machinery are safe, properly maintained, and functioning efficiently.
  • Provide coaching and training on job assignments, standards, and customer service, demonstrating correct procedures and adherence to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).
  • Conduct quality checks to ensure services meet UCF standards and process guidelines.
  • Coordinate and schedule safety and tree care-related training for the team.
  • Ensure compliance with safety standards, address medical needs in case of injury, and document all accidents, injuries, and unsafe conditions.
  • Promote and maintain a strong safety culture within the unit.
  • Review work orders and projects for accuracy, ensuring all timelines and details are met.
  • Act as a resource for technical guidance and problem resolution.
  • Serve as a team leader for vegetative debris removal during natural disasters, such as hurricanes and tropical storms, overseeing the safe and efficient removal of fallen trees, branches, and other vegetation.

Minimum Qualifications:

High school Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of arboricultural experience overseeing tree care projects including pruning, removals, and disease management in an institutional or large-scale setting, such as a university, park system, or municipality.
  • Previous leadership roles overseeing tree care teams or related operations.
  • Experience with advanced tree care techniques, such as cabling, bracing, and lightning protection systems.
  • Proficiency in operating and maintaining specialized tree care equipment, including aerial lifts and root remediation tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills for customer interaction, report preparation, and team coordination.
  • Experience implementing safety protocols and conducting safety training sessions.
  • Prior experience coordinating tree care or debris removal efforts during or after natural disasters, including hurricanes or tropical storms.

Health Assessment Required:  

UCF policy requires completion and passing of a physical exam for this position.


Special Instructions to the Applicants:

The anticipated salary range for this position is $23.33 to $31.21. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


Sign-On Bonus: This position may be eligible for a sign-on bonus based on applicable criteria.


The selected candidate will be required to obtain an ISA Certified Arborist credential within six months of hire. The cost of certification will be covered by the department.


Position requires a valid class E driver’s license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.


May be required to participate in respiratory, medical examination and training in use of respirators.


All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
