jobs.description_text:
The VP Pharmacy Services is the senior-most pharmacy executive for the enterprise and reports to the Chief Operating Officer, Health Services. This transformational leader articulates a clear and compelling vision for pharmacy, drives innovation, inspires others, and sets high expectations for achievement within and beyond the pharmacy organization. The role serves as the trusted pharmacy advisor to the executive leadership team and the Board.
This position holds strategic, operational, and financial accountability for all Commercial and Medicare pharmacy and specialty pharmacy programs at a Blue plan with approximately $30 billion in annual revenue. Accountabilities include enterprise pharmacy cost of care and multi-year trend, benefit and formulary strategy, Pharmacy Benefit Manager (PBM) performance, Medicare Part D and Commercial regulatory compliance, and clinical quality outcomes. The role is accountable for achieving and sustaining Part D Star Ratings of 4.5 stars or higher across the organization’s Medicare Advantage prescription drug and stand-alone Part D contracts; for delivering pharmacy savings as a core contributor to total cost of care and affordability goals, with specialty and medical-benefit drug trend as a primary focus; and for leading the renegotiation and restructuring of PBM and specialty pharmacy arrangements while building a strong pharmacy operations organization that manages vendors and clinical programs.
 Integrating pharmacy and medical strategy is essential to improving quality and controlling total cost of care. The VP Pharmacy Services leads the integration of clinical and operational solutions across the pharmacy and medical benefits to deliver innovative, cross-functional, and compliant programs.
This executive aligns team operational and budget goals with organizational directives, acts as a change leader within and beyond Pharmacy and Health Services, and provides organization-wide direction for project and functional resources inside and outside the reporting structure. Additional responsibilities include applying rigorous controls and oversight to the PBM and other strategic vendors across Pharmacy and Health Services to ensure compliance with all contractual terms and all State and Federal regulations.
 Key Responsibilities: 
Pharmacy Strategy and Operations:
• Build, develop, and lead a diverse, high-performing pharmacy leadership team and organization that applies individual expertise to collectively achieve organizational goals and objectives
• Set the enterprise pharmacy vision and multi-year strategy for Commercial (individual, small group, large group, and ASO) and Medicare lines of business, delivering a coordinated, comprehensive pharmacy program that supports member care and aligns with the company’s vision and strategic imperatives
• Own pharmacy cost of care for the enterprise, including multi-year pharmacy trend forecasting, budget accountability for multi-billion-dollar pharmacy spend, and delivery of net-cost and rebate targets, and accountable for annual pharmacy savings targets as a core contributor to enterprise total cost of care and affordability goals, with savings validated using enterprise methodology and reported separately as realized versus avoided
• Lead the annual goal, budget, and financial planning process, ensuring goals are timely, measurable, and executed
• Monitor pharmacy cost and trend continuously to identify operational improvement and savings opportunities
• Direct PBM strategy and governance, including RFP and market-check activities, contract negotiation, pricing, rebate and performance guarantee terms, transparency and audit rights, and ongoing performance management to secure best-in-market net cost and member experience, with specific accountability to lead the renegotiation of PBM agreements informed by independent market-check results and the design and execution of restructured specialty pharmacy arrangements, including carve-out and multi-vendor models, ensuring seamless member transition, data integration, and protection of rebate and performance guarantees
• Oversee the PBM and other pharmacy vendors across Commercial and Medicare to ensure contractual performance and achievement of the organization’s strategic imperatives, using scorecards and governance that cover performance guarantees, claims pricing accuracy, audit findings closure, rebate guarantee attainment and collection, and service levels, and pursuing financial remedies for non-performance
• Lead pharmacy operations across the full operating cycle, including formulary and clinical policy administration, pharmacy coverage determinations and appeals, medical-benefit drug management (prior authorization, dose optimization, wastage, and infusion site of care), dispensing channel and network strategy, claims pricing and payment accuracy, and rebate invoicing, collection, and reconciliation
• Lead pharmacy clinical programs, including adherence, Medication Therapy Management, medication safety, and prescriber engagement, and the outreach vendors that support them, ensuring each program has defined objectives and measured ROI
• Set formulary, benefit design, and clinical pharmacy program strategy, including oversight of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) process, to balance clinical outcomes, affordability, and member access
• Lead specialty drug strategy across the pharmacy and medical benefits, including site-of-care, biosimilar adoption, specialty network and vendor strategy, and management of emerging high-cost therapies such as GLP‑1s and cell and gene therapies, with accountability for specialty and medical-benefit drug trend, including exclusive specialty network utilization, infusion site of care, dose optimization and wastage reduction, and rebate capture
• Direct Medicare Part D strategy and operations in partnership with Actuary and Medicare leadership, including annual bid development, formulary and network adequacy, Medication Therapy Management, and readiness for Inflation Reduction Act requirements, including the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan and Maximum Fair Price
• Own Part D Star Ratings performance, with a goal of 4.5 stars or higher for each Medicare Advantage prescription drug (HMO and PPO) contract and stand-alone Part D contract, including medication adherence, statin use in persons with diabetes, Medication Therapy Management comprehensive medication reviews, and medication safety measures, in partnership with Quality and Medicare leadership
• Integrate Commercial and Medicare pharmacy programs with medical strategy to reduce total cost of care while achieving quality outcomes
• Build and deliver a pipeline of pharmacy affordability initiatives (for example, formulary and tiering, alternative sourcing, site of care, and manufacturer agreements), partnering with Healthcare Economics, Analytics, and Finance to quantify and validate savings
• Lead pharmacy innovation, including manufacturer value-based agreements, digital and point-of-care pharmacy solutions, and alternative sourcing and pricing models, and evaluate their impact on total cost of care and member experience
• Partner with Product and Actuary to deliver competitive, innovative Commercial and Medicare pharmacy product offerings in the marketplace
• Support targeted ASO efforts to ensure competitiveness, growth, and financially positive outcomes
• Lead the design and implementation of targeted interventions to improve pharmacy trend and support membership growth while minimizing disenrollment
• Partner with Analytics and Healthcare Economics to build pharmacy performance reporting, forecasting, and drug trend analytics that inform executive decision-making
• Establish and own pharmacy operations and clinical KPI scorecards, with leading and lagging indicators reported through the Health Services management rhythm
• Apply data, automation, and AI (such as electronic prior authorization and predictive adherence and cost-risk modeling) to improve turnaround, outcomes, and efficiency
• Lead the transformation of Commercial, Medicare, and specialty pharmacy to support future and changing health care models
Executive Leadership and Enterprise Representation:
• Serve as the enterprise pharmacy executive, advising the executive leadership team and Board on pharmacy strategy, drug trend, and regulatory developments, and partnering with BCBSA, peer Blue plans, manufacturers, and industry coalitions
• Represent Florida Blue and Health Care Services, both internally and externally, on pharmacy and related regulatory matters, including BCBSA activity and proposed State and Federal legislation, leveraging key relationships and professional organizations to influence policy and industry peers
• Lead team operational efforts to minimize risk and ensure compliance with all Commercial and Medicare pharmacy State and Federal regulations, including coverage determination and appeal turnaround, CMS program audit readiness, Part C and Part D reporting requirements, and evolving federal PBM transparency requirements
• Continuously evaluate internal and external factors that pose pharmacy-related risk to Florida Blue, and develop and implement controls and operational processes to mitigate that risk
• Provide ongoing support, input, and oversight to Health Care Services (HCS) strategic partnerships
• Lead the development and implementation of Healthcare Solutions through key initiatives, including High-Value initiatives pursued with Network and through IMM Governance
• Develop effective partnerships with key leaders in Sales/Marketing, Compliance, Medical Operations, Care Management, Service Organization, Network, Product, and Legal
• Remain current on issues affecting the pharmacy industry and integrate best practices to manage them effectively
• Lead diverse, multi-disciplinary, cross-functional teams to support organizational goals and directives, providing direct and indirect leadership to GuideWell Health Solutions by leveraging individual and team expertise
Clinical Support and Oversight:
• Oversee pharmacy-related committees, including Pharmacy and Therapeutics and pharmacy policy, and ensure alignment with medical policy for drugs covered under the medical benefit
• Oversee the review and implementation of selected enabling technologies, tools, and initiatives, using organizational SMEs and support staff, that promote quality, administrative efficiency, and medical cost goals
• Provide clinical oversight of pharmacy and drug-related medical policies to ensure clinical integration and alignment, and provide leadership and direction to achieve effective clinical programs and operational excellence, with a focus on member outcomes
 Key Requirements: 
• Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) or related PhD or additional equivalent senior executive experience considered
• 15+ years’ of progressive related work experience in health care, health plan, or PBM leadership
• Health Plan/PBM senior leadership Executive leadership of enterprise pharmacy operations
• 10+ years of progressive management experience, including leading managers and senior leaders
• Pharmacist License - current Florida pharmacy license or able to obtain
• Deep knowledge of the health care and insurance industry and of managed care products, benefits, and programs, including Commercial and Medicare
• Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, including executive and Board-level presentation

• Demonstrated ability to build productive, collaborative working relationships with key internal and external stakeholders
• Demonstrated knowledge and application of the Florida Blue Management System
• Demonstrated knowledge and application of the profession of pharmacy, including clinical pharmacy, Florida pharmacy law, and the process flow for prescription drug services in Florida
• Demonstrated success improving Medicare Part D Star Ratings, including medication adherence, Medication Therapy Management, and medication safety measures
• Experience leading PBM RFPs and negotiating PBM and specialty pharmacy contracts, including pricing, guarantees, and rebates

• Experience overseeing pharmacy operations and vendor performance at scale, including prior authorization, claims accuracy, and rebate management

jobs.title: Executive Assistant to the CEO
jobs.description_html:
The Executive Assistant to the CEO is a strategic, high-judgment member of the Office of the CEO. This role goes well beyond calendar and logistics. It helps run the CEO's office: anticipating what is coming, connecting the dots across the enterprise, protecting and directing the CEO's time and attention toward what matters most, and making sure the CEO is prepared for colleagues, the Board and external partners. The role uses modern technology, including AI tools, to run the office with speed, efficiency, accuracy and consistency, and works as a close partner to the Chief of Staff and the Office of the CEO team.

Who We Are Looking For:
We are looking for a dynamic, curious and highly capable partner who moves at the pace of a fast-moving CEO. You will anticipate needs, spot where the dots need to be connected, use sound judgment about where the CEO's time is best spent, and keep colleagues, leaders and Board members well served and well informed. You are comfortable using AI tools to automate routine work and sharpen drafts, which frees your time for the judgment calls only a trusted partner can make. You bring discretion, composure under pressure and genuine care for the experience of the people who work with the CEO.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic partnership and anticipation  
•    Act as a day-to-day operating partner to the CEO and the Office of the CEO: anticipate priorities, manage the flow of work, and keep the office running proactively rather than reactively.
•    Connect the dots across the enterprise. Recognize when a conversation, decision, deadline or risk in one area affects another, and flag it to the CEO and Chief of Staff with a recommendation, not just a heads-up.
•    Prepare the CEO with a regular look ahead: what is coming, what needs a decision, and what is at risk.
Time and priorities  
•    Manage the CEO's calendar as a strategic tool. Use judgment to prioritize, protect focus time and decide where the CEO's time and presence matter most.
•    Filter meeting requests: accept those that are needed, decline or pass on others, and elevate to the Chief of Staff anything that needs a discussion.
•    Make sure each meeting has the right people, preparation and purpose, and that agendas and pre-reads reach participants in time.
Inbox and communications  
•    Triage and manage the CEO's inbox and incoming requests, many confidential or sensitive. Draft replies for the CEO’s review, route and prioritize the rest, and summarize what needs the CEO’s attention.
•    Pull out items that need a conversation, especially speaking invitations and requests for the CEO's endorsement or presence, and review them with the Chief of Staff before they go to the CEO.
•    Working closely with the dedicated communications resource, draft, edit and proofread CEO correspondence in the CEO's voice, in plain and clear language, for CEO review. 
Technology and AI  
•    Use technology and AI tools to run the office: build and improve workflows, templates, trackers and knowledge systems; automate routine tasks; and share what works with the Office of the CEO team.
•    Follow GuideWell's guidelines for handling confidential, Board and protected information in any tool.
Colleague and Board experience  
•    Support the experience of colleagues and Board members in their interactions with the CEO. Prepare the CEO for Board and executive engagements and coordinate the CEO's own participation and travel.
•    Stay closely attuned to the CEO's meetings with the Board Chair: know the timing, who needs to know about it, and what the CEO will need beforehand.
•    Partner closely with the Board Services leader, who owns the Board calendar, portal and logistics. Stay connected on Board schedules and on the CEO's review of Board materials so the CEO's time is set aside when it is needed.
•    Work as part of a tight team with the Chief of Staff, the Chief of Staff's executive assistant, and the dedicated communications resource, so that the CEO and Board members experience one coordinated office.
The CEO’s other board service  
•    Proactively manage the CEO’s service on other boards. Keep a long-range view of meeting cycles, committee meetings and key dates, and protect time well in advance, including around the GuideWell Board calendar.
•    Own the preparation timeline for those boards: track material deadlines and pre-reads, prepare the CEO with briefing notes and open items, and raise conflicts and risks early.
•    Work hand in hand with the dedicated communications resource on remarks, talking points and written materials for those boards, so the CEO’s materials are consistent, polished and on time.
•    Follow-through and office operations  
•    Track commitments and follow up with leaders and departments on assignments, decisions and deadlines. Bring forward what is slipping before it becomes a problem.
•    Complete or lead special projects, and manage office operations including budget, time and expense reporting, and filing and records systems.
•    Interact with individuals at all levels inside and outside the Company, including Board members, with professionalism, discretion and strict confidentiality

What Success Looks Like:
•    The CEO arrives at every meeting on time and prepared.
•    The CEO's calendar reflects his stated priorities, with protected time for strategy and for people.
•    Routine work runs with little CEO involvement, and the office is measurably faster because of the workflows and tools this person builds.
•    Commitments made by or to the CEO are tracked and closed on time.
•    The CEO's other board commitments are planned well ahead, and materials are ready before deadlines.

Key Requirements: 
•    7+ years of progressively responsible experience supporting senior executives, ideally a CEO or C-suite leader.
•    Track record of exercising judgment, handling confidential information and acting independently.
•    Advanced Microsoft Office skills (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams) and experience with adopting new technology, including AI tools.
•    Ability to anticipate needs, prioritize competing demands and use sound judgment on behalf of a senior executive.
•    Project management experience, with the ability to plan, coordinate and drive multiple initiatives and deadlines to completion across teams.
•    Ability to connect the dots across the enterprise, recognizing how developments in one area affect another and bringing forward recommendations, not just observations.
•    Ability to work flexible hours to meet business needs, including occasional evenings.
•    Ability to travel as required, 10% or less, including Board-related travel.
•    Hands-on experience using AI tools, automation or workflow technology to streamline executive support.
•    Exceptional discretion, emotional intelligence and the ability to build trust and influence with leaders at every level.
•    Self-starter who raises issues and offers recommendations without being asked.
•    Bachelor’s degree preferred or equivalent related work experience.

Preferred:
•    Experience supporting a CEO or Board of Directors, including Board meeting preparation and communications.
•    Experience in healthcare, insurance or another regulated and complex enterprise.
•    Strong business writing and editing skills, including writing in plain, clear language and in another person’s voice.

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: Maintenance Technician II - Riverside Office Complex, Nights/Weekends
jobs.description_html:
The Maintenance Technician works independently under moderate supervision, performs planned and corrective maintenance on electrical, HVAC, mechanical, life safety, and plumbing systems. Operates industrial HVAC systems, including chillers, cooling towers, air handlers and pumps. Operates life safety systems, including fire alarm and suppression systems. Incumbents are not permitted to deviate from standard practices and procedures, but may be permitted to set priorities, subject to supervisory approval.

Important to Know

  • Must be able to work flexible shifts that will include weekends

  • This role with have multiple shifts

    • 2 shifts 11pm Friday - 11PM Saturday & 11PM Saturday to 11AM Sunday

    • 2 shifts 11pm Sunday - 7am Monday & 11pm Monday - 7am Tuesday

What You Will Be Doing

  • Perform preventive maintenance on building engineering systems. 
  • Diagnose and perform corrective maintenance on building engineering systems. 
  • Build, modify, and repair furniture per provided drawings. Conduct large room setups for conferences. 
  • Operate and repair HVAC, mechanical, life safety, electrical and plumbing systems. 
  • Monitor vendor’s performance of major equipment systems maintenance 
  • Perform light carpentry and electrical work such as painting, drywall repairs and ballast changes. 
  • Monitor and operate critical facilities equipment using Automated Building Management System and inform management of any abnormalities discovered. 

What We Require

  • 3+ years related work experience in: building systems (HVAC, electro-mechanical, etc.) maintenance and repair 

  • High school diploma or GED 

  • Knowledge of chiller plant operations and basic maintenance of HVAC systems. 

  • Knowledge of basic electrical operations and maintenance. 

  • Experience reading blueprints and Mechanical, Electrical and plumbing plans. 

  • Experience with pump, bearing, and fan motor replacements

  • Experience Identifying and replacing faulty plumbing components. 

  • Experience working on a computer in a Windows environment. 

  • Must meet the requirements to be classified as a Regular Driver in accordance with Vehicle Use Policy Number 4.16. 

  • Must be able to work variable shifts, night, and weekend shift rotations, including overtime and holidays.

What We Prefer

  • Experience with emergency generating systems. 

  • Experience with Automated Building Management Systems. 

  • Knowledge of UPS systems and operations. 

  • Experience with HVAC equipment repairs 

  • Experience with troubleshooting and repair of industrial kitchen equipment. 
     

General Physical Demands

  • Heavy work: Exerting up to 100 pounds of force occasionally and/or up to 50 pounds of force frequently. 
     

Physical/Environmental Activities

  • Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences).

  • Occasionally May be exposed to outdoor weather conditions of cold, heat, wet, and humidity.

  • Frequently May be exposed to outdoor or warehouse conditions of loud noises, vibration, fumes, dust, odors, and mists. 

  • Frequently Must be able to ascend and descend ladders, stairs, or other equipment. 

What We Offer


As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and a comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases.

Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $38

jobs.title: Sr Director Performance Advisory Services
jobs.description_html:
The Principal Experience Advisor leads the enterprise experience advisory portfolio and prioritization across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services, spanning nine customer dimensions: employees, prospects, members, patients, providers, family caregivers, brokers/agents, plan sponsors, and vendor partners. This role also owns the end-to-end improvement, design, and co-execution of personalized, relevant, and consistent experiences and signature moments, and sets organizational standards for experience practice, while ensuring all initiatives drive measurable business results. This leader is responsible for making significant improvement in publicly reported outcomes (e.g., MA-CAHPS, HOS) and business priorities (e.g., retention, NPS, trust). By maturing human-centered design principles and practice within the team and throughout the organization, this role facilitates the adoption of future-leaning skills to help deliver an unmatched, world-class experience. 
 

This leader builds a high-performing team that operates as a core function within a shared service model, supporting enterprise-wide strategic efforts across business units and other shared services. While maturing the team from a people, process, and technology perspective, this leader must also create the conditions for experience-obsessed teams and be bold in how we pioneer work that is first of its kind, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders. This function sits within the 'business product' team and works hand-in-hand with the 'technology product' teams. This is a senior leader role reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Customer Experience & Engagement.
 

Key Responsibilities:
Portfolio & Strategy
•    Own the complete experience advisory portfolio across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services, including the prioritized book of member/customer/provider/broker journeys and their associated value-at-stake.
•    Define and communicate the “why, how, what” narrative for all experience initiatives and enterprise-wide activation efforts.
•    Establish and enforce ROI expectations on all deliverables, ensuring accountability for measured outcomes rather than recommendations alone.
•    Maintain a cohesive portfolio of current work, future work, and net-new innovations.
 

Design & Delivery Standards
•    Set the design-and-delivery methodology and standards for the practice, including journey design, service design, and touchpoint redesign.
•    Ensure that solutions are designed once, deployed, and then scaled across the enterprise.
•    Co-develop the capability hub—a centralized repository of best-in-class tools, templates, and resources—to enable enterprise-wide adoption and consistency.
 

Team Leadership & Development
•    Lead a high-performing, nimble, and agile team of experience advisors and experience operations leads.
•    Build deep bench strength through mentoring, capability development, and cross-functional pairing.
•    Hold team members accountable for advocating for the member/customer/patient perspective in all work.
•    Develop partnerships with top MBA and BA schools for internships and fellowships to create a strong pipeline of talent.
•    Champion a culture of experience obsession—democratizing human-centered design methods and tools so that business and frontline teams can apply them consistently across the enterprise.
 

Operations & Governance
•    Oversee Customer Experience (CX) business unit pods, quality standards, and operational seams.
•    Maintain disciplined 2×2 prioritization (time to value) for all experience work and enforce work-in-progress caps to prevent overload.
•    Ensure experience improvements are tied to measured results and business outcomes.
 

Key Requirements:
•    10+ years related work experience in customer experience, service design, or related strategic advisory roles.
•    Demonstrated success leading enterprise-wide experience or transformation initiatives across multiple business lines.
•    Proven expertise in journey mapping, service design, and customer-centric methodologies.
•    Strong track record of translating experience improvements into measurable business results and ROI.
•    Experience building and scaling high-performing teams in complex, matrixed environments.
•    Excellent communication skills with ability to influence stakeholders at all levels.
•    5+ years direct supervisory/management experience
•    Related Bachelor's degree or additional related equivalent work experience
 

Preferred:
•    Certification in design thinking, service design, or related disciplines.
•    Experience with agile and lean methodologies.
•    Familiarity with CX technology platforms and analytics tools.
•    Prior experience managing cross-functional pods or business units.
•    Track record of building reusable capability hubs or centers of excellence.
•    Experience with healthcare, insurance, or banking administration. 
 

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living.

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 

•    Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
•    Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
•    Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
•    Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
•    Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
•    Additional voluntary benefits available; and
•    A comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases.

Annualized Salary Range: $180,000 - $292,500

Typical Annualized Hiring Range: $180,000 - $236,250

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: Sr Director Precision Engagement
jobs.description_html:
The Principal Engagement Orchestration leads the enterprise contact strategy and engagement orchestration engine that delivers the right message, through the right channel, at the right moment—without overwhelming the people we serve. This role encompasses nine customer dimensions: employees, prospects, members, patients, providers, family caregivers, brokers/agents, plan sponsors, and vendor partners. This role designs and manages enterprise-wide customer communication strategies and execution plans, guided by "N of 1" personalization and "Self-Service first" principles. This role owns cross-channel communication governance, frequency capping, and suppression logic across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements while maximizing engagement effectiveness. 
 

The Principal Engagement Orchestration serves as the strategic steward of the member communications portfolio, balancing discretionary outreach with mandatory touchpoints, and drives measurable improvements in reach, opt-out rates, and contact-load management. This leader builds a high-performing team that operates as a core function within a shared service model, supporting enterprise-wide strategic efforts across business units and other shared services. While maturing the team from a people, process, and technology perspective, this leader must also create the conditions for experience-obsessed teams and be bold in how we pioneer work that is first of its kind, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders. This function sits within the 'business product' team and works hand-in-hand with the 'technology product' teams. This is a senior leader role reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Customer Experience & Engagement.
 

Key Responsibilities:
Enterprise Contact Strategy & Governance
•    Own the enterprise contact strategy across all channels (letter, call, IVR, email, SMS/text, push in-app and web) and across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services.
•    Define the enterprise communication strategy and channel selection logic and lead the team that turns them into execution plans.
•    Own the enterprise customer communication calendar and sequencing across business units, so no member receives conflicting or stacked messages.
•    Govern frequency capping, suppression rules, sequencing, and prioritization logic to protect members from communication overload.
•    Enforce compliance across regulatory, brand, and preference requirements, including HIPAA, TCPA, CAN-SPAM, and CMS Medicare marketing and communications guidelines.
•    Own customer preference and consent management, ensuring every communication honors what the member has opted into.
•    Establish and monitor the contact-load metric; hold accountability for reducing unnecessary contact burden while maintaining engagement effectiveness.
•    Balance regulatory-required communications with discretionary outreach, ensuring compliance and member preference respect.
 

Engagement Logic & Channel Standards
•    Set next-best-action sequencing logic and channel-mix standards that optimize member experience and engagement outcomes.
•    Define rules and decision trees that determine optimal timing, channel, and message sequencing for each member segment and journey stage.
•    Ensure consistency and quality across all channels, touchpoints, and outbound communications while maintaining flexibility for business unit and segment-specific needs.
•    Ensure all customer-facing messages are clear, consistent, timely, and delivered through the optimal channel, adhering to “N of 1” personalization and “Self-Service first” principles.
•    Monitor for communication fatigue and duplication, and prevent them before they reach the member.
 

Communications Portfolio & Narrative
•    Own the engagement narrative and the member communications portfolio across all business units.
•    Curate and govern the portfolio of outbound messages, campaigns, and touchpoints to ensure coherence, relevance, and non-redundancy.
•    Partner with key stakeholders (product, marketing, operations, business units) to align communications strategy with broader experience and business objectives.
•    Partner with Marketing on campaign orchestration, so campaigns run through the same frequency, sequencing, and suppression rules as all other outreach.
•    Collaborate with Experience Advisory (journey and content design) and UX/UXR (look and feel) to define communication templates.
 

Integration & Closed-Loop Accountability
•    Partner with the Principal Experience Intelligence, who owns the targeting, signal, and predictive models, and own how those models are governed and operationalized within the engagement strategy to close the loop between insights and engagement actions.
•    Provide regular feedback to Product on communication effectiveness, including what drives response, self-service adoption, and opt-outs.
•    Ensure that engagement orchestration is informed by real-time data, member preferences, and predictive signals.
•    Drive accountability for engagement effectiveness metrics: reach, response rates, opt-out rates, message fatigue, and contact-load reduction.
•    Translate engagement performance into actionable insights for continuous improvement.
 

Team Leadership & Development
•    Lead a mixed, high-performing team of orchestration strategists and engagement leads.
•    Build deep bench strength through mentoring, capability development, and cross-functional pairing.
•    Foster expertise in orchestration platforms, engagement strategy, and member-centric communication design.
•    Develop partnerships with top MBA and BA schools for internships and fellowships to create a strong pipeline of talent.
•    Champion a culture of experience obsession—democratizing engagement rules and contact-load visibility so that every outreach decision protects the member from overload.
 

Key Requirements:
•    10+ years related work experience in customer engagement, marketing operations, contact center strategy, or related fields. 
•    Demonstrated success designing and governing enterprise-wide contact strategies across multiple channels and business lines.
•    Proven expertise in frequency capping, suppression logic, and engagement orchestration.
•    Strong background in regulatory compliance (HIPAA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, state-specific regulations) as it relates to member communications.
•    Experience leading cross-functional teams in complex, matrixed environments.
•    Track record of reducing contact overload and improving engagement effectiveness metrics.
•    Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills with ability to influence at all organizational levels
•    5+ years direct supervisory/management experience
•    Related Bachelor's degree or additional related equivalent work experience
 

Preferred Qualifications:
•    Experience in healthcare, insurance, benefits industry, or banking administration.
•    Expertise in marketing automation platforms, orchestration engines, or customer journey platforms.
•    Experience with contact center operations, IVR systems, or omnichannel communication strategies.
•    Familiarity with member preference management and consent/suppression frameworks.
•    Knowledge of advanced analytics, A/B testing, and engagement optimization methodologies.
•    Experience with agile engagement planning or rapid campaign deployment.
•    Track record building governance frameworks or centers of excellence for communications.
•    Certification in marketing, customer experience, or related disciplines.
 

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally

•    Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;

jobs.description_text:
The Principal Engagement Orchestration leads the enterprise contact strategy and engagement orchestration engine that delivers the right message, through the right channel, at the right moment—without overwhelming the people we serve. This role encompasses nine customer dimensions: employees, prospects, members, patients, providers, family caregivers, brokers/agents, plan sponsors, and vendor partners. This role designs and manages enterprise-wide customer communication strategies and execution plans, guided by "N of 1" personalization and "Self-Service first" principles. This role owns cross-channel communication governance, frequency capping, and suppression logic across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements while maximizing engagement effectiveness. 
 The Principal Engagement Orchestration serves as the strategic steward of the member communications portfolio, balancing discretionary outreach with mandatory touchpoints, and drives measurable improvements in reach, opt-out rates, and contact-load management. This leader builds a high-performing team that operates as a core function within a shared service model, supporting enterprise-wide strategic efforts across business units and other shared services. While maturing the team from a people, process, and technology perspective, this leader must also create the conditions for experience-obsessed teams and be bold in how we pioneer work that is first of its kind, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders. This function sits within the 'business product' team and works hand-in-hand with the 'technology product' teams. This is a senior leader role reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Customer Experience & Engagement.
 Key Responsibilities: 
Enterprise Contact Strategy & Governance
• Own the enterprise contact strategy across all channels (letter, call, IVR, email, SMS/text, push in-app and web) and across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services.
• Define the enterprise communication strategy and channel selection logic and lead the team that turns them into execution plans.
• Own the enterprise customer communication calendar and sequencing across business units, so no member receives conflicting or stacked messages.
• Govern frequency capping, suppression rules, sequencing, and prioritization logic to protect members from communication overload.
• Enforce compliance across regulatory, brand, and preference requirements, including HIPAA, TCPA, CAN-SPAM, and CMS Medicare marketing and communications guidelines.
• Own customer preference and consent management, ensuring every communication honors what the member has opted into.
• Establish and monitor the contact-load metric; hold accountability for reducing unnecessary contact burden while maintaining engagement effectiveness.
• Balance regulatory-required communications with discretionary outreach, ensuring compliance and member preference respect.
 Engagement Logic & Channel Standards
• Set next-best-action sequencing logic and channel-mix standards that optimize member experience and engagement outcomes.
• Define rules and decision trees that determine optimal timing, channel, and message sequencing for each member segment and journey stage.
• Ensure consistency and quality across all channels, touchpoints, and outbound communications while maintaining flexibility for business unit and segment-specific needs.
• Ensure all customer-facing messages are clear, consistent, timely, and delivered through the optimal channel, adhering to “N of 1” personalization and “Self-Service first” principles.
• Monitor for communication fatigue and duplication, and prevent them before they reach the member.
 Communications Portfolio & Narrative
• Own the engagement narrative and the member communications portfolio across all business units.
• Curate and govern the portfolio of outbound messages, campaigns, and touchpoints to ensure coherence, relevance, and non-redundancy.
• Partner with key stakeholders (product, marketing, operations, business units) to align communications strategy with broader experience and business objectives.
• Partner with Marketing on campaign orchestration, so campaigns run through the same frequency, sequencing, and suppression rules as all other outreach.
• Collaborate with Experience Advisory (journey and content design) and UX/UXR (look and feel) to define communication templates.
 Integration & Closed-Loop Accountability
• Partner with the Principal Experience Intelligence, who owns the targeting, signal, and predictive models, and own how those models are governed and operationalized within the engagement strategy to close the loop between insights and engagement actions.
• Provide regular feedback to Product on communication effectiveness, including what drives response, self-service adoption, and opt-outs.
• Ensure that engagement orchestration is informed by real-time data, member preferences, and predictive signals.
• Drive accountability for engagement effectiveness metrics: reach, response rates, opt-out rates, message fatigue, and contact-load reduction.
• Translate engagement performance into actionable insights for continuous improvement.
 Team Leadership & Development
• Lead a mixed, high-performing team of orchestration strategists and engagement leads.
• Build deep bench strength through mentoring, capability development, and cross-functional pairing.
• Foster expertise in orchestration platforms, engagement strategy, and member-centric communication design.
• Develop partnerships with top MBA and BA schools for internships and fellowships to create a strong pipeline of talent.
• Champion a culture of experience obsession—democratizing engagement rules and contact-load visibility so that every outreach decision protects the member from overload.

• 10+ years related work experience in customer engagement, marketing operations, contact center strategy, or related fields. 
• Demonstrated success designing and governing enterprise-wide contact strategies across multiple channels and business lines.
• Proven expertise in frequency capping, suppression logic, and engagement orchestration.
• Strong background in regulatory compliance (HIPAA, CAN-SPAM, TCPA, state-specific regulations) as it relates to member communications.

jobs.title: Sr Director VOC Intelligence
jobs.description_html:
The Principal Experience Intelligence will lead the evolution and design of the Voice of the Customer (VOC) Intelligence function, shaping enterprise-wide capabilities that propel the organization forward. The function includes enterprise always-on listening, predictive intelligence/data science, and B2B and B2C research and insight teams that inform business decisions and capabilities to help GuideWell serve each person as a unique individual. The Principal Experience Intelligence is accountable for translating raw data and signals into prioritized, actionable insights—moving the organization from reactive reporting to predictive intelligence for a unique individual within their own context and life stage—as well as for target setting, performance optimization, and the persistent evolution of our intelligence strategy. This role encompasses nine customer dimensions: employees, prospects, members, patients, providers, family caregivers, brokers/agents, plan sponsors, and vendor partners. 
 

This leader builds a high-performing team that operates as a core function within a shared service model, supporting enterprise-wide strategic efforts across business units and other shared services. While maturing the team from a people, process, and technology perspective, this leader must also create the conditions for experience-obsessed teams and be bold in how we pioneer work that is first of its kind, working hand-in-hand with stakeholders. Ensuring data integrity, model governance, and enterprise adoption of analytics capabilities to inform product development and experience optimization is a foundational expectation for success in this role. This function sits within the 'business product' team and works hand-in-hand with the 'technology product' teams. This is a senior leader role reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Customer Experience & Engagement.
 

Key Responsibilites:
Strategy & Activation
•    Own the unified, end-to-end experience and engagement insight strategy as part of the enterprise experience strategy, business product priorities, and conditions of engagement.
•    Build and maintain an always-on listening strategy that captures all nine dimensions while prioritizing member, prospect, and patient feedback across all touchpoints and channels.
•    Design and evolve the unified profile to support personalization, segmentation, and targeted interventions.
•    Develop the framework and lead the process for turning VoC and market intelligence into prioritized, evidence-backed product opportunities that support core stakeholders across Health Services, Commercial and Government Markets, and Shared Services, along with the ability to measure downstream impact on satisfaction, retention, and revenue.
•    Own the models that enable real-time, data-driven decision-making across the enterprise, partnering with the Principal Engagement Orchestration, who governs and operationalizes them within the engagement strategy, to achieve both the aspirations of the people we serve and our business objectives.
 

Analytics, Insights & Reporting
•    Lead the development, production, and delivery of insight briefs tied to internal and external data sources and research to inform the business cycle.
•    Set analytics and data-science methodology and standards for the organization.
•    Maintain a multi-stakeholder research calendar focused on insights, market trends, and current member trends across Commercial and Government Markets (including Medicare and ACA), Health Services/care delivery, and marketing that stays ahead of each business cycle.
•    Own predictive models (e.g., CAHPS, HOS, Retention, NPS) and ensure their accuracy, relevance, and production deployment.
•    Develop and scale personalization capabilities to deliver a rich profile that enhances individualized experiences.
•    Translate complex data signals into prioritized, business-ready insights; hold accountability for the percent of enterprise decisions backed by data.
 

Experience Surveillance & Prediction
•    Develop the roadmap for an Experience Surveillance System designed to uncover experience fatigue, unmet needs, broken promises, and populations/people being left behind or stuck within a digital channel.
•    Move the function from reactive insights to predictive intelligence; proactively flag at-risk individuals and journeys before survey data confirms problems.
•    Reduce signal-to-insight cycle time and increase the velocity of insight delivery to decision-makers.
Vendor & Ecosystem Rationalization
•    Assess and rationalize the insights, VoC, and brand tracking vendor ecosystem across all brands, working with procurement, IT, and CMX operations to consolidate fragmented contracts, renegotiate strategic partnerships, and build a streamlined technology portfolio that delivers maximum enterprise value.
•    Evaluate and implement best-in-class platforms across VoC, consumer research, and marketing and brand measurement.
 

Data Governance & Adoption
•    Govern experience data integrity through endorsements, stewardship, and cross-functional communication.
•    Ensure data coverage across all business units, member segments, and touchpoints.
•    Drive adoption of predictive models and analytics tools in production environments.
•    Establish data quality standards and accountability mechanisms across the enterprise.
 

Team Leadership & Development
•    Lead a mixed, high-performing team of analysts, data scientists, and sub-function leads.
•    Build deep bench strength through mentoring, capability development, and cross-functional pairing.
•    Foster a data-driven culture and champion the use of evidence in decision-making.
•    Develop partnerships with top MBA and BA schools for internships and fellowships to create a strong pipeline of talent.
•    Champion a culture of experience obsession—democratizing insights by making them accessible to frontline teams and senior leaders alike, so that every decision is grounded in evidence.
 

Key Requirements:
•    10+ years related work experience in data analytics, data science, or business intelligence.
•    Demonstrated expertise in building and scaling data foundations, data warehouses, or analytics platforms.
•    Strong background in predictive modeling, statistical analysis, and machine learning.
•    Proven success developing and deploying production analytics models (e.g., churn prediction, NPS, retention).
•    Experience leading cross-functional teams of analysts and data scientists in complex, matrixed environments.
•    Deep understanding of customer experience metrics, listening strategies, and voice-of-customer programs.
•    Excellent communication skills with ability to translate technical insights into business language for executive audiences.
•    5+ years direct supervisory/management experience
•    Related Bachelor's degree or additional related equivalent work experience

Preferred:
•    Experience in healthcare, insurance, benefits industry, or banking administration.
•    Advanced degree in data science, statistics, computer science, or related field.
•    Expertise in real-time analytics, streaming data, or event-driven architecture.
•    Experience with customer data platforms (CDPs), marketing automation, or member engagement platforms.
•    Familiarity with orchestration engines, rules engines, or decisioning systems.
•    Track record building Experience Surveillance Systems or similar proactive monitoring frameworks.
•    Certification in data science, analytics, or related disciplines.
•    Experience with agile analytics or rapid insight delivery methodologies.
 

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living.

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 

•    Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
•    Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
•    Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
•    Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
•    Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
•    Additional voluntary benefits available; and
•    A comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases.

Typical Annualized Hiring Range: $180,000 - $236,250

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

jobs.title: Human Resources Advisor II
jobs.description_html:
The HR Advisor will answer incoming calls, emails and chats and provide HR process information and guidance to employees and managers, Includes first contact case resolution utilizing the HR Knowledgebase and general understanding of HR policies/programs. HR support includes benefits, compensation, employee relations, employee self-service, enterprise learning, manager self-service, performance management and staffing. 
The HR Advisor will manage the overall resolution of incoming calls and will triage initial calls and open and manage cases that require additional research and expertise. The HR advisor will perform other HR administrative support for HR transactions into HR systems and perform additional functions including and not limited to keying position data and related actions, Candidate Expenses, Tuition Assistance and other HR administrative processes.

Key Responsibilities: 
Online Functions
•    Demonstrate broad HR knowledge, as pertains to the various Guidewell companies, providing employees with relevant information, policy explanation and self-service navigation support.
•    Perform intake of HR inquiries via case management, telephone, chat or email. Will assess inquiries or reported issues to determine best method of resolution. 
•    Triage call based upon inquiry to determine level of urgency and specific issue
•    Utilize knowledgebase and general knowledge to support issues resolution, provide counsel or identify when case escalation is appropriate. 
•    Provide high-touch employee service that meets expected service levels and business performance goals. 
•    Coach callers in the use of self-service.
•    Document inquiries within the case management tool, transfer case to next tier or direct caller to third party vendor if appropriate.
•    Provide follow up communication to employees to ensure satisfaction and case resolution.
•    Properly document employee contact information and employee notes regarding interaction
Offline Functions
•    Keys compensation and position data, including new hire information, promotional increases, position updates and related actions into an automated human resources’ system. 
•    Creates, updates, purges and otherwise maintains active employee files. Retrieves employee records for authorized requestors. Ensures terminated employee files are purged when appropriate and that the Company’s records management policy is adhered to at all times.
•    Perform transactional and administrative work and data entry as required while maintaining data and system integrity
•    Support the integrity of employee records and HR data. 
Benefits & Compliance Support
•    Monitor weekly and monthly reports to correct errors as needed or escalate to HRIS.
•    Conduct benefits sessions for new hire classes.
•    Ensure new hires, re-hires, and transfers are enrolled accurately and in a timely manner.
•    Assists new hires with onboarding – login issues and Token IDs.
•    Plan and promote annual biometric screening clinics across 2 Texas locations.
•    Track and report on wellness program participation metrics, identifying trends and opportunities for improvement.
•    Partner with the pharmacy team to organize annual vaccine clinic sessions at convenient times and locations.
•    Track clinic participation.
•    Provide additional support where needed.
Process/Continuous Improvement
•    Works collaboratively within a team to share ideas, ownership, and accountability for driving improvements and consistency of execution for key HR processes.
•    Provide feedback on employee issues and the knowledgebase so that management can address and improve tools.
•    Participate in scheduled and ad hoc training in order to improve policy and process acumen.
•    Identify and report any call trends or product trends to the HR Solutions Center Manager.
•    Support mass mail initiatives, open enrollment and special projects, as assigned

Job Requirements: 
•    4+ years’ related work experience. Experience Details: Human resources, customer service, or related experience of which 1-2 years of it being in Human Resources or related functional or generalist experience 
•    High school diploma or GED 
•    Demonstrated working knowledge with Microsoft Office products is required (Word, Excel, Outlook) 
•    Demonstrated strong interpersonal, verbal (phone) and written communication, as well as active listening skills to handle a volume of inbound inquiries from employees; position continually requires demonstrated poise, tact and diplomacy
•    Ability to travel occasionally

Preferred:
•    Knowledge of HR policies and procedures
•    Knowledge of HR systems associate or bachelor’s degree in related field HR Certification, PHR, SHRM Experience working with HRIS System (Peoplesoft/Oracle), Taleo, Skillsoft, SuccessFactors
•    Prior experience in multiple functional areas of Human Resources (for example, staffing, compensation, benefits)
 

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 
 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally 

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

  • Attend and host external events promoting center activities while fostering community relationships.

jobs.title: Claims Examiner I
jobs.description_html:
Get To Know Us!

WebTPA, a GuideWell Company, is a healthcare third-party administrator with over 30+ years of experience building unique benefit solutions and managing customized health plans.

Key position details: 

  • Anticipated Training Class Start Date:  12/7/2026
  • Schedule Monday to Friday 8:00am - 4:30pm Central Time for 4 weeks

What is your impact?
As a Claim Examiner, you will handle processing and adjudication for healthcare claims. This will include claims research where applicable and a range of claim complexity. 

What Will You Be Doing: 

  • Day-to-day processing of claims for accounts:
    • Responsible for processing of claims (medical, dental, vision, and mental health claims)
    • Claims processing and adjudication.
    • Claims research where applicable. 
    • Reviews and processes insurance to verify medical necessities and coverage under policy guidelines (clinical edit logic).
    • Incumbents are expected to meet and/or exceed qualitative and quantitative production standards.
  • Investigation and overpayment administration:
    • Facilitate claims investigation, negotiate settlements, interpret medical records, respond to Department of Insurance complaints, and authorize payment to claimants and providers.
    • Overpayment reviews and recovery of claims overpayment; corrected financial histories of patients and service providers to ensure accurate records.
    • Utilize systems to track complaints and resolutions. 
  • Other responsibilities include resolving claims appeals, researching benefits, verifying correct plan loading. 

What You Must Have: 

  • 2+ years related work experience.
  • Claims examiner/adjudication experience on a computerized claims payment system in the healthcare industry.
  • High school diploma or GED 
  • Knowledge of CPT and ICD-10 coding required. 
  • Knowledge of COBRA, HIPAA, pre-existing conditions, and coordination of benefits required. 
  • Must possess proven judgment, decision-making skills and the ability to analyze. 
  • Ability to learn quickly and multitask.
  • Proficiency in maintaining good rapport with physicians, healthcare facilities, clients and providers. 
  • Concise written and verbal communication skills required, including the ability to handle conflict. 
  • Proficiency using Microsoft Windows and Word, Excel and customized programs for medical CPT coding. 
  • Review of multiple surgical procedures and establishment of reasonable and customary fees.

What We Prefer: 

  • Some college courses in related fields are a plus.
  • Other experience in processing all types of medical claims helpful. 
  • Data entry and 10-key by touch/sight 

What We Can Offer YOU!

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As a WebTPA employee, you will have access to:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, Short- and long-term disability programs
  • Flexible schedules after training + WAH options! 
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances.
  • Retirement Savings Plan includes employer contribution and employer match
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, and 11 holidays
  • Additional voluntary benefits available and a comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for interns and part-time employees may differ.

  • Anticipated Training Class Start Date:  12/7/2026
  • Schedule Monday to Friday 8:00am - 4:30pm Central Time for 4 weeks

What is your impact?
As a Claim Examiner, you will handle processing and adjudication for healthcare claims. This will include claims research where applicable and a range of claim complexity. 

What Will You Be Doing: 

  • Day-to-day processing of claims for accounts:
    • Responsible for processing of claims (medical, dental, vision, and mental health claims)
    • Claims processing and adjudication.
    • Claims research where applicable. 
    • Reviews and processes insurance to verify medical necessities and coverage under policy guidelines (clinical edit logic).
    • Incumbents are expected to meet and/or exceed qualitative and quantitative production standards.
  • Investigation and overpayment administration:
    • Facilitate claims investigation, negotiate settlements, interpret medical records, respond to Department of Insurance complaints, and authorize payment to claimants and providers.
    • Overpayment reviews and recovery of claims overpayment; corrected financial histories of patients and service providers to ensure accurate records.
    • Utilize systems to track complaints and resolutions. 
  • Other responsibilities include resolving claims appeals, researching benefits, verifying correct plan loading. 

What You Must Have: 

  • 2+ years related work experience.
  • Claims examiner/adjudication experience on a computerized claims payment system in the healthcare industry.
  • High school diploma or GED 
  • Knowledge of CPT and ICD-10 coding required. 
  • Knowledge of COBRA, HIPAA, pre-existing conditions, and coordination of benefits required. 
  • Must possess proven judgment, decision-making skills and the ability to analyze. 
  • Ability to learn quickly and multitask.
  • Proficiency in maintaining good rapport with physicians, healthcare facilities, clients and providers. 
  • Concise written and verbal communication skills required, including the ability to handle conflict. 
  • Proficiency using Microsoft Windows and Word, Excel and customized programs for medical CPT coding. 
  • Review of multiple surgical procedures and establishment of reasonable and customary fees.

What We Prefer: 

  • Some college courses in related fields are a plus.
  • Other experience in processing all types of medical claims helpful. 
  • Data entry and 10-key by touch/sight 

What We Can Offer YOU!

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As a WebTPA employee, you will have access to:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, Short- and long-term disability programs
  • Flexible schedules after training + WAH options! 
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances.
  • Retirement Savings Plan includes employer contribution and employer match
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, and 11 holidays
  • Additional voluntary benefits available and a comprehensive wellness program

jobs.title: Assistant General Counsel - Procurement & Technology Transactions
jobs.description_html:
The successful candidate in this mid-level attorney position will provide legal counsel and transactional support for procurement, healthcare operations, technology transactions, and strategic business initiatives across GuideWell and its affiliated companies. With 5-10 years of relevant legal experience, this role requires experience in commercial contracting and complex vendor, healthcare, and technology transactions.

The incumbent will support health insurance, provider, and health solutions businesses and work closely with procurement, business, technology, privacy, compliance, information security, and operational stakeholders. This position provides legal advice and counsel on complex commercial matters with limited supervision and requires sound business judgment and independent decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:
•    Draft, review, and negotiate commercial agreements, including master services agreements, statements of work, software licenses, SaaS and cloud agreements, professional and consulting services agreements, data use agreements, business associate agreements, and strategic arrangements.
•    Provide legal support for procurement activities and supplier relationships across payer, provider, and health solutions business operations.
•    Advise business clients regarding contractual, healthcare regulatory, operational, and legal risks associated with healthcare services, technology solutions, and third-party engagements.
•    Support transactions involving software, artificial intelligence, analytics, interoperability, data licensing, cybersecurity, and other technology-enabled healthcare solutions.
•    Advise on intellectual property matters related to commercial transactions, including ownership of deliverables, licensing rights, confidentiality, trademarks, copyrights, and use of third-party materials.
•    Collaborate with procurement, privacy, compliance, information security, technology, and business teams to identify and mitigate legal and business risks.
•    Conduct legal research and analysis and prepare memoranda, presentations, contract analyses, and other legal documentation.
•    May assume additional legal responsibilities and special projects as needed to support organizational objectives and the broader legal department.

Key Requirements:
•    Juris Doctorate degree from an accredited law school with a strong academic record and 5-10 years of professional legal experience.
•    Admission to at least one state bar. If bar admission is in a state other than Florida, then the ability to be certified in Florida as Authorized House Counsel.
•    Experience supporting healthcare, managed care, provider, health solutions, healthcare technology, or related healthcare businesses.
•    Demonstrated experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating complex commercial agreements.
•    Experience supporting procurement, vendor contracting, healthcare transactions, technology transactions, or other sophisticated business operations.
•    Strong knowledge of contract law, commercial transactions, and risk allocation principles.
•    Working knowledge of intellectual property concepts and technology transaction documents, including software licensing and ownership of deliverables.
•    Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex legal and regulatory concepts to non-attorney audiences.
•    Strong organizational, negotiation, and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
•    Sound professional judgment and demonstrated ability to provide practical, business-focused legal advice.
•    Demonstrated initiative, self-motivation, and ability to work independently with limited supervision.

Preferred:
•    Experience supporting both payer and provider-side business operations.
•    Experience negotiating software, SaaS, cloud, data licensing, artificial intelligence, digital health, or other technology transactions.
•    Prior experience with a nationally recognized law firm.
•    Prior in-house counsel experience.
•    Familiarity with healthcare privacy, data governance, information security, and regulatory compliance requirements.
•    At least one professional certification from the International Association of Privacy Professionals (IAPP), such as Artificial Intelligence Governance Professional (AIGP), Certified Information Privacy Professional/United States (CIPP/US), Certified Information Privacy Manager (CIPM), or Certified Information Privacy Technologist (CIPT).

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 


What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Annualized Salary Range: $136,000 - $221,000

Typical Annualized Hiring Range: $136,000 - $170,000

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.
