jobs.title: VP Quality and Accreditation
jobs.description_html:
The Vice President, Quality & Accreditation is the enterprise executive accountable for clinical quality performance across all lines of business, including Medicare and Commercial. This role owns HEDIS strategy and operations, accreditation (NCQA, URAC, and applicable state/federal standards), clinical quality programs, and the vendor ecosystem that supports HEDIS data collection, abstraction, and reporting.

This executive unifies quality functions historically siloed by line of business into a single operating model, ensuring consistent measurement, documentation, and improvement practices across Medicare and Commercial populations.

The role is accountable for HEDIS rates and audit results, accreditation status and survey outcomes, clinical quality program performance, and vendor ecosystem governance and cost.

Key Responsibilities: 
Enterprise Quality Leadership & Operating Model
•    Build a unified quality operating model across all lines of business, including Medicare and Commercial.
•    Establish enterprise governance for clinical documentation integrity supporting quality measurement.
•    Serve as the executive owner of enterprise HEDIS performance and accreditation status.
•    Oversee all HEDIS operations, hybrid strategy, supplemental data, and provider documentation improvement, across Medicare and Commercial lines of business.
•    Develop best-in-class intervention playbooks for each HEDIS measure.
Clinical Quality
•    Lead enterprise clinical quality programs, including quality improvement initiatives, clinical practice guideline adoption, and provider quality performance programs.
•    Ensure alignment with care management and population health functions on shared clinical priorities.
•    Partner with COO, CFO, Network, Pharmacy, Stars, Risk Adjustment, and Operations leadership to ensure quality initiatives are coordinated enterprise-wide without assuming accountability for their respective programs.
Accreditation
•    Own enterprise accreditation strategy and execution, including NCQA Health Plan Accreditation, URAC, and other applicable state and federal accreditation or certification requirements.
•    Lead survey readiness, documentation, and corrective action planning for all accreditation activities.
•    Maintain accreditation standards as they evolve and ensure organizational readiness for renewal cycles.
HEDIS Vendor Ecosystem Leadership
•    Serve as the executive owner of the vendor ecosystem supporting HEDIS data collection, medical record retrieval, abstraction, and supplemental data.
•    Consolidate and manage HEDIS vendors to reduce cost, improve data quality, and strengthen audit defensibility.
•    Establish unified SLAs, KPIs, and performance governance for HEDIS-related vendors.
•    Ensure vendors operate as extensions of the internal quality team.
Quality Analytics, Reporting & Forecasting
•    Ensure data quality, timeliness, and integration across clinical, operational, and vendor systems supporting quality measurement.
•    In partnership with Health Services Analytics, build a unified reporting architecture for HEDIS, accreditation, and clinical quality programs.
Governance & Compliance
•    Ensure compliance with NCQA, URAC, and applicable regulatory requirements governing quality and accreditation.
•    Lead enterprise audit readiness for HEDIS and accreditation surveys.
•    Establish governance structures for decision-making, escalation, and cross-functional alignment on quality matters.

Key Requirements:
•    10+ years of leadership experience in health plan Quality, HEDIS, and Accreditation, across Medicare and Commercial lines of business.
•    Bachelor's degree in healthcare administration, public health, business, or related field preferred.
•    Proven track record of improving HEDIS rates and achieving strong NCQA/URAC accreditation outcomes.
•    Deep knowledge of HEDIS technical specifications, NCQA accreditation standards, and clinical quality improvement methodology.
•    Experience leading large cross-functional teams and complex vendor ecosystems, particularly HEDIS data and abstraction vendors.
•    Strong financial acumen, including forecasting, ROI analysis, and budget management.
•    Demonstrated ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide change.
•    Master's degree in healthcare administration, public health, business, or related field preferred.

General Physical Demands: Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will thrive in our Be Well, Work Well, GuideWell culture where being well as an individual, and working well as a team, are both important in serving our members and communities. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 

•    Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
•    Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
•    Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
•    Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
•    Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
•    Additional voluntary benefits available; and
•    A comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.description_html:
All of our team members and contributors are expected to deliver results with accountability while collaborating seamlessly across boundaries. They embrace change with resilience, staying curious and learning continuously in a rapidly evolving landscape. Grounded in business understanding and comfortable with AI and digital tools, they solve problems with critical thinking and creativity. Above all, they are driven to serve—ensuring their work creates meaningful impact for members and the community we support.

For leadership roles, we seek individuals who think critically, embrace a future-focused mindset, and bring intentional perspective to their work —whether managing people, leading projects, or guiding teams. Our ideal candidates operate across matrix environments, applying systems thinking and evidence-based decision-making to drive sustainable results with economic discipline. We value those who lead change with courage and conviction, building trust across teams, and orchestrating both human and AI capabilities to amplify impact. Across all roles - managing direct reports, leading projects, or advancing individual expertise - they cultivate resources, strengthen capabilities, and create conditions for people and work to thrive. Above all, they are committed to building durable value—decisions and actions today that compound organizational strength tomorrow.

 

Job Summary
Critical leadership role responsible for setting technology strategy and architecture direction for Engagement Technology. Drives cloud migration, architectural simplification, and AI adoption across products and engineering practice. Partners with Enterprise Architecture, the AI COE, Data COE, Security, and peer engineering leaders. Must be credible with engineers and persuasive with executives.

Key Requirements

  • Engagement Technology strategy and architecture: drive the target-state architecture across product, platform, and integration domains; lead solution architecture for major initiatives; drive architectural simplification and legacy retirement; establish architecture governance and the design review process; and translate business strategy into technical direction.

  • Enterprise collaboration and influence: serve as the primary interface to Enterprise Architecture; partner with the AI Engineering, Data, Security, and Infrastructure COEs; represent the group in enterprise architecture forums; and build relationships with peer leaders to secure alignment.

  • AI SDLC transformation: own the AI SDLC transformation within Engagement Technology; select, pilot, and scale AI engineering tooling; establish standards, guardrails, and secure usage patterns; define and track adoption and productivity measures; and drive enablement, training, and change management.

  • Cloud migration and modernization: own the cloud migration strategy and execution roadmap; define migration patterns and target cloud architecture; partner with Infrastructure, Security, and FinOps; and provide executive visibility into progress and cost.

  • Leadership: lead and grow a high-caliber team, mentor senior engineers and architects, and operate as a member of the Engagement Technology leadership team. 

Qualifications

  • 7+ years related work experience in software engineering and architecture, including enterprise-wide scope for the Senior Director level. 

  • Deep hands-on technical skills across web and mobile, API and event-driven integration, iPaaS, identity, and cloud-native architecture.

  • Demonstrated ownership of target-state architecture in a multi-product environment.

  • Experience leading cloud migration and modernization programs.

  • Practical experience applying AI to the software development lifecycle.

  • Proven ability to influence across Enterprise Architecture, Security, and Infrastructure organizations.

  • Credible with engineers and persuasive with executives.

Required Management Experience

  • 5+ years direct supervisory/management experience 
     

Required Education

  • Related Bachelor’s degree or additional related equivalent work experience Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent combination of education and experience considered. 
     

Preferred Education

  • Master’s degree Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical discipline. 
     

Preferred Qualifications

  • 15+ years of Software engineering and architecture, including enterprise-wide scope for the Senior Director level. 

  • 5+ years Leading architecture or technical transformation at scale. 

  • 10+ years of Hands-on cloud experience (AWS preferred), including cloud-native, web/mobile, API and event integration, iPaaS, and identity. 

  • Healthcare, insurance, or other regulated industry experience. 

  • AI/ML platform and GenAI solution architecture experience. 

  • Experience with AWS Bedrock and Snowflake Cortex. 

  • FinOps practices and cloud cost management.

  • Business or platform transition and integration experience.

jobs.title: Sr Director - Office of the CEO
jobs.description_html:
The Sr Director Office of the CEO (OCEO) serves as a trusted operator and advisor to a C-suite executive, providing organizational leadership support to advance business growth, innovation, performance, and operational excellence.

The Sr Director will drive key initiatives and projects forward, track requests from the CEO and SVP Chief of Staff through to completion, and work across the Executive Leadership Team (ELT) and the broader organization. The role operates as an extension of the executive, driving clarity, operational discipline, organizational alignment, and measurable business performance.

Key Responsibilities: 
Executive Support & Advisory: 
•    Translates direction and enterprise priorities into clear action items with defined owners, deadlines, and next steps
•    Represent the OCEO in enterprise forums and with ELT members as needed
•    Own the intake, tracking, and closure of requests and action items from the CEO and SVP Chief of Staff, maintaining a single source of truth with owners, due dates, and status
•    Drive accountability for goal achievement, performance metrics, and continuous improvement 
•    Prioritize and sequence competing requests in partnership; escalate blockers and at-risk items before they become problems
•    Capture decisions and commitments from CEO and ELT meetings, communicate them clearly, and monitor downstream execution
Project & Initiative Execution:
•    Keep CEO priority initiatives and projects moving forward by managing plans, milestones, dependencies, and status, and by stepping in hands-on wherever needed to drive progress
•    Serve as executive liaison to ELT members and cross-functional teams to resolve issues, remove barriers, and ensure successful implementation of company initiatives
•    Support and convene cross-functional teams for planning, development, and execution of key initiatives
•    Identify and mitigate risks that could impact financial performance, operational stability, or organizational reputation
•    Analyze data and distill it into concise, fact-based summaries and options for the CEO and ELT
Communication & Engagement:
•    Communicate executive decisions clearly and monitor downstream execution
•    Plan and execute leadership forums, town halls, and strategic summits
•    Prepare and oversee executive presentations for internal and external audiences
•    Support the CEO's operating cadence, including ELT meetings, monthly and quarterly operating reviews, and board of directors’ preparation, through agendas, pre-reads, materials, and follow-up
•    Facilitate leadership meetings and develop executive-level content as needed
•    Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, inclusivity, and engagement aligned with enterprise values, and support leadership and talent efforts in partnership with HR as needed

Key Requirements:
•    10+ years of progressive experience in operations, program management, strategic planning, consulting, finance, or related fields within complex organizations
•    Bachelor's degree in related discipline or additional related work experience
•    Proven ability to turn priorities and direction into disciplined, on-time execution
•    Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and tenacious follow-through
•    Ability to manage many competing priorities and fast-changing requests simultaneously without losing sight of the details
•    Sound business judgment and enterprise-level business acumen, with the ability to serve as a credible advisor to senior leadership
•    Strong executive presence with the ability to influence and drive accountability among senior stakeholders and decision-makers without direct authority
•    Advanced project and program management expertise
•    Demonstrated success operating in ambiguous, fast-paced environments
•    Strong financial literacy and understanding of operational drivers 
•    Skilled at diagnosing issues early and mobilizing resources to resolve them
•    Highly facilitative leadership style with strong interpersonal effectiveness
•    Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite
•    Exceptional discretion and ability to handle confidential information. Strong ownership mindset and results orientation
•    Ability to respectfully challenge assumptions and elevate decision quality

Preferred:
•    Master's degree
•    Knowledge of the health care industry
•    Experience in a Fortune 500 or similarly complex, highly matrixed enterprise
•    Prior experience in a chief of staff, office of the CEO, program management office, enterprise transformation, or operational excellence role
•    Experience with change management and organizational effectiveness
•    Exposure to executive-level governance processes and enterprise planning cycles


General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 
 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally 

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will thrive in our Be Well, Work Well, GuideWell culture where being well as an individual, and working well as a team, are both important in serving our members and communities. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Annualized Salary Range: $168,000 - $273,000

Typical Annualized Hiring Range: $168,000 - $210,000

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: IT Summer 2027 Undergraduate Internship
jobs.description_html:
Florida Blue 2027 IT Summer Internship Program

Florida Blue's Remote IT Summer Internship program is designed to give college juniors, seniors, and graduate students a hands-on look at our business processes and the tech systems that power them. You'll work on real projects, get on-the-job training, and partner with a mentor from your track-specific team.

In addition to your daily responsibilities, you'll have opportunities to:

  • Meet with leaders from all domains within the Tech organization
  • Engage with Executive Tech Leadership throughout the program
  • Present to Florida Blue's CIO and Tech Vice Presidents at the program's conclusion

We pride ourselves on a culture that values flexibility, innovation, and diversity. Bring your unique talents and help us advance our mission of helping people and communities achieve better health.

Read more about the tracks offered below and the qualifications/requirements for each.

Generative AI

You'll dive deep into the world of applied generative AI at GuideWell — working hands-on with enterprise AI platforms to design, build, and deploy solutions that solve real business problems. From prompt engineering and agentic workflows to tool integrations and responsible AI practices, you'll collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to bring AI capabilities to life across the organization.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A strong foundation in how large language models work, including prompting techniques, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic/tool-use patterns
  • Experience with LLM APIs and application frameworks (e.g., LangChain, or similar orchestration tools); experience with open-source or commercial models is a plus
  • Proficiency in Python; familiarity with ML/DL frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch is a plus but not required
  • Data manipulation and statistical analysis skills
  • Curiosity about responsible and effective AI adoption — how to evaluate, govern, and scale AI solutions in a business setting, not just build them
  • A passion for generative AI that drives you to push boundaries and explore new possibilities

A background in Computer Science, Computer or Electrical Engineering, AI/ML, Data Science, Mathematics/Statistics, etc. is preferred.

Infrastructure

As an Infrastructure intern, you'll help in the development and implementation of policies and procedures to safeguard our company data, databases, and information systems. You'll be the one who keeps our technology secure, efficient, and running at peak performance.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A knack for designing, implementing, and troubleshooting technology
  • Experience in monitoring and maintaining complex systems
  • A passion for keeping our digital kingdom safe and secure
  • The skills to develop and implement policies that protect our tech assets

Basic skills/experience:

  • Knowledge or experience with AI platforms, LLMs, or supporting AI infrastructure/integrations is a plus
  • Knowledge of Linux commands and understanding of how to work with Linux boxes
  • Basic understanding of OpenShift and Kubernetes

Cloud Engineering

As a Cloud Services intern, you'll delve into the world of infrastructure as code, networking, automation, data storage, and security, using industry-leading platforms like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A curious and adventurous spirit, always eager to learn and explore
  • A willingness to take on new challenges and push the boundaries of what's possible
  • A passion for cloud computing and its endless possibilities
  • The drive to stay ahead of the curve and master the latest cloud technologies
  • Experience with AWS or Azure is preferred

Cybersecurity

As a Cybersecurity intern, you'll have the chance to work alongside the best in the business, tackling real-world challenges and projects that make a real difference.

You'll be part of a top-notch cybersecurity organization, collaborating with highly skilled red-team and blue-team members who are experts in their field. Together, you'll take on the toughest security challenges, using your skills and knowledge to outsmart cyber threats and protect our digital assets. You'll explore multiple security frameworks, stay ahead of the curve, and work on developing a deep understanding of information security concepts, principles, and solutions.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A passion for cybersecurity and a desire to make a real impact
  • A strong foundation in information security principles and practices
  • The drive to stay ahead of cyber threats and protect our digital world
  • Interest in how AI-assisted tools are changing threat detection and response is a plus

Completed or in-progress certifications such as Security+, Network+, A+, and/or Linux+ preferred.

Data Analytics

As a Data Analytics intern, you'll work on real-world business problems and publicly available datasets, applying cutting-edge techniques like data wrangling, model development, and visualization.

You'll be focused on data analytics, business intelligence, and data quality assessment for Florida Blue, working to drive business growth and improve health outcomes.

To succeed in this role, you'll need to be:

  • Passionate and inquisitive, always seeking to learn and improve
  • A quick learner, able to adapt to new tools and techniques
  • An expert "Googler," able to find creative solutions to complex problems
  • Have basic skills in SQL, R, and/or Python

Data Science

As a Data Science intern, you will have the opportunity to work on real-world projects, collaborate with experienced data scientists and engineers, and contribute to the development of innovative data analytics solutions. Responsibilities include designing, developing, and deploying data analytics models and algorithms to solve business problems, and analyzing large datasets to identify trends, patterns, and insights.

Key skills required include knowledge of machine learning algorithms, deep learning techniques, data analysis, and visualization, as well as strong collaboration and communication skills.

To be successful in this role, you are required to be:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Computational Biology
  • Skilled in programming languages such as Python, R, or SQL
  • Analytical, detailed, and able to work with large datasets
  • Taking high-level computer science and math courses, such as Data Structures and Algorithms, Calculus I, Probability and Statistics, Linear Algebra, Calculus II

Application Development

As an application developer, you'll have the chance to showcase your creative skills, leveraging your knowledge of web development, design, and programming to craft solutions that make a real impact.

You'll focus on developing new applications, exploring new technologies, and pushing the boundaries of what's possible. You'll need excellent communication skills to collaborate with teams, gather requirements, and design solutions that meet business needs.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • Strong programming skills in languages like Java, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Python, or Swift
  • Knowledge of database management systems such as MySQL, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL
  • Experience with version control systems like Git
  • Experience with front-end frameworks such as React or Angular
  • Familiarity with back-end frameworks such as Node.js
  • A finger on the pulse of current technology trends and a desire to stay ahead of the curve

Business Analyst

As a Business System Analyst intern, you'll define and document business requirements, as well as collaborate with software developers, product owners, and testers to bring innovative solutions to life.

You'll help with end-to-end capabilities and assist in guiding projects from concept to production deployment. With your troubleshooting skills, you'll identify and resolve application defects, ensuring that business and end-user needs are met.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A strong understanding of business operations and processes
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex problems into manageable parts
  • Experience with business analysis tools and techniques, such as use cases, user stories, and process mapping
  • Familiarity with software development methodologies, such as Agile and Waterfall
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams
  • Experience with SQL databases is preferred

Must Have’s:

  • Currently enrolled in computer science, information technology, mathematics, psychology, or related degree program as a Junior or Senior student at an accredited college/university 
  • Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better
  • Must be able to commit to working at least 30 hours a week
  • Basic PC skills required including working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook)
  • Basic programming knowledge, JavaScript/HTML/CSS or other Object Oriented programming experience
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; team and collaboration-oriented
  • Work under minimal supervision and adapt to a dynamic, changing environment

  • Must be a creative and innovative thinker

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $38

Typical Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $30

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 IT Graduate Internship
jobs.description_html:
Florida Blue 2027 IT Summer Internship Program

Florida Blue's Remote IT Summer Internship program is designed to give college juniors, seniors, and graduate students a hands-on look at our business processes and the tech systems that power them. You'll work on real projects, get on-the-job training, and partner with a mentor from your track-specific team.

In addition to your daily responsibilities, you'll have opportunities to:

  • Meet with leaders from all domains within the Tech organization
  • Engage with Executive Tech Leadership throughout the program
  • Present to Florida Blue's CIO and Tech Vice Presidents at the program's conclusion

We pride ourselves on a culture that values flexibility, innovation, and diversity. Bring your unique talents and help us advance our mission of helping people and communities achieve better health.

Read more about the tracks offered below and the qualifications/requirements for each.

Generative AI

You'll dive deep into the world of applied generative AI at GuideWell — working hands-on with enterprise AI platforms to design, build, and deploy solutions that solve real business problems. From prompt engineering and agentic workflows to tool integrations and responsible AI practices, you'll collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to bring AI capabilities to life across the organization.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A strong foundation in how large language models work, including prompting techniques, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic/tool-use patterns
  • Experience with LLM APIs and application frameworks (e.g., LangChain, or similar orchestration tools); experience with open-source or commercial models is a plus
  • Proficiency in Python; familiarity with ML/DL frameworks like TensorFlow or PyTorch is a plus but not required
  • Data manipulation and statistical analysis skills
  • Curiosity about responsible and effective AI adoption — how to evaluate, govern, and scale AI solutions in a business setting, not just build them
  • A passion for generative AI that drives you to push boundaries and explore new possibilities

A background in Computer Science, Computer or Electrical Engineering, AI/ML, Data Science, Mathematics/Statistics, etc. is preferred.

Infrastructure

As an Infrastructure intern, you'll help in the development and implementation of policies and procedures to safeguard our company data, databases, and information systems. You'll be the one who keeps our technology secure, efficient, and running at peak performance.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A knack for designing, implementing, and troubleshooting technology
  • Experience in monitoring and maintaining complex systems
  • A passion for keeping our digital kingdom safe and secure
  • The skills to develop and implement policies that protect our tech assets

Basic skills/experience:

  • Knowledge or experience with AI platforms, LLMs, or supporting AI infrastructure/integrations is a plus
  • Knowledge of Linux commands and understanding of how to work with Linux boxes
  • Basic understanding of OpenShift and Kubernetes

Cloud Engineering

As a Cloud Services intern, you'll delve into the world of infrastructure as code, networking, automation, data storage, and security, using industry-leading platforms like Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A curious and adventurous spirit, always eager to learn and explore
  • A willingness to take on new challenges and push the boundaries of what's possible
  • A passion for cloud computing and its endless possibilities
  • The drive to stay ahead of the curve and master the latest cloud technologies
  • Experience with AWS or Azure is preferred

Cybersecurity

As a Cybersecurity intern, you'll have the chance to work alongside the best in the business, tackling real-world challenges and projects that make a real difference.

You'll be part of a top-notch cybersecurity organization, collaborating with highly skilled red-team and blue-team members who are experts in their field. Together, you'll take on the toughest security challenges, using your skills and knowledge to outsmart cyber threats and protect our digital assets. You'll explore multiple security frameworks, stay ahead of the curve, and work on developing a deep understanding of information security concepts, principles, and solutions.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A passion for cybersecurity and a desire to make a real impact
  • A strong foundation in information security principles and practices
  • The drive to stay ahead of cyber threats and protect our digital world
  • Interest in how AI-assisted tools are changing threat detection and response is a plus

Completed or in-progress certifications such as Security+, Network+, A+, and/or Linux+ preferred.

Data Analytics

As a Data Analytics intern, you'll work on real-world business problems and publicly available datasets, applying cutting-edge techniques like data wrangling, model development, and visualization.

You'll be focused on data analytics, business intelligence, and data quality assessment for Florida Blue, working to drive business growth and improve health outcomes.

To succeed in this role, you'll need to be:

  • Passionate and inquisitive, always seeking to learn and improve
  • A quick learner, able to adapt to new tools and techniques
  • An expert "Googler," able to find creative solutions to complex problems
  • Have basic skills in SQL, R, and/or Python

Data Science

As a Data Science intern, you will have the opportunity to work on real-world projects, collaborate with experienced data scientists and engineers, and contribute to the development of innovative data analytics solutions. Responsibilities include designing, developing, and deploying data analytics models and algorithms to solve business problems, and analyzing large datasets to identify trends, patterns, and insights.

Key skills required include knowledge of machine learning algorithms, deep learning techniques, data analysis, and visualization, as well as strong collaboration and communication skills.

To be successful in this role, you are required to be:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, Physics, or Computational Biology
  • Skilled in programming languages such as Python, R, or SQL
  • Analytical, detailed, and able to work with large datasets
  • Taking high-level computer science and math courses, such as Data Structures and Algorithms, Calculus I, Probability and Statistics, Linear Algebra, Calculus II

Application Development

As an application developer, you'll have the chance to showcase your creative skills, leveraging your knowledge of web development, design, and programming to craft solutions that make a real impact.

You'll focus on developing new applications, exploring new technologies, and pushing the boundaries of what's possible. You'll need excellent communication skills to collaborate with teams, gather requirements, and design solutions that meet business needs.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • Strong programming skills in languages like Java, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, Python, or Swift
  • Knowledge of database management systems such as MySQL, MongoDB, or PostgreSQL
  • Experience with version control systems like Git
  • Experience with front-end frameworks such as React or Angular
  • Familiarity with back-end frameworks such as Node.js
  • A finger on the pulse of current technology trends and a desire to stay ahead of the curve

Business Analyst

As a Business System Analyst intern, you'll define and document business requirements, as well as collaborate with software developers, product owners, and testers to bring innovative solutions to life.

You'll help with end-to-end capabilities and assist in guiding projects from concept to production deployment. With your troubleshooting skills, you'll identify and resolve application defects, ensuring that business and end-user needs are met.

To succeed in this role, you'll need:

  • A strong understanding of business operations and processes
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down complex problems into manageable parts
  • Experience with business analysis tools and techniques, such as use cases, user stories, and process mapping
  • Familiarity with software development methodologies, such as Agile and Waterfall
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams
  • Experience with SQL databases is preferred

Must Have’s:

  • Currently enrolled in computer science, information technology, mathematics, psychology, or related Master degree program at an accredited college/university 
  • Cumulative GPA of 3.0 or better
  • Must be able to commit to working at least 30 hours a week
  • Basic PC skills required including working knowledge of Microsoft Office products (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook)
  • Basic programming knowledge, JavaScript/HTML/CSS or other Object Oriented programming experience
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; team and collaboration-oriented
  • Work under minimal supervision and adapt to a dynamic, changing environment

  • Must be a creative and innovative thinker

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $38

Typical Hourly Pay Range: $24 - $30

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: RN Case Manager
jobs.description_html:
Get To Know Us!

WebTPA, a GuideWell Company, is a healthcare third-party administrator with over 30+ years of experience building unique benefit solutions and managing customized health plans.

What is your impact?

The RN Case Manager primary responsibility is to create, implement, and monitor treatment plans to assist patients/members in meeting their healthcare goals. You would use knowledge of healthcare and social services to assess needs and provide interdisciplinary care options in treatment planning for the member. This would include understanding the member's healthcare benefits and healthcare best practices needed for effective treatment planning.

Key Job Details: 

  • Hours Monday to Friday ability to work 9a-6p CST or 10a-7p CST shift required
  • California RN state license 

What Will You Be Doing: 

  • Case Management process includes assessing the member’s health status and care coordination needs. Can include inpatient review and discharge planning, as well as possible outpatient management. 
  • Contact with patient, family, physicians, additional health care providers, and community resources. Contact with provider business offices and with the employer/client may also be required. 
  • Identification of alternative treatment plans, which would have to be approved by all parties. These alternative care plans will be based on quality care within cost containment guidelines, allowing available claims dollars to be used in the most judicious manner possible. 
  • Assessment of the clinical status and resultant sequela to coordinate the most appropriate service to meet the individual’s health care needs. The Case Manager will then monitor the health status and the impact of the treatment plan for each client. The Case Manager will be responsible for altering the care plan as deemed appropriate by the dynamic, ever-changing client needs. 
  • Identification of services, resources, providers, and facilities that could best serve members in a timely and cost-effective manner, to promote optimum value for the client and reimbursement source. 
  • Development and implementation of Case Management goals, both short and long term, with documented care plans. 
  • Utilize technology/resources to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of the elected treatment plan, pre-implementation and post-implementation. This outcome measurement will be used in determining the effective results and in establishing future patient-centered care plans. 
  • Accurate and timely reporting as deemed appropriate by each client member. 
  • Medical record review to determine medical necessity of requested services. 
  • Interpreting individual health plans and authorizing/coordinating care in accordance with plan provisions. 

What You Must Have:

  • 5+ years related work experience with a professional background in clinical nursing and patient assessment. 
  • Related Bachelor’s degree or additional related equivalent work experience 
  • Graduate of an accredited school of nursing 
  • RN - Registered Nurse - State Licensure 
  • Knowledgeable in medical terminology, reasonable and necessary treatment plans, delivery quality health care services and cost containment practices.
  • Ability to collaborate with cross-operational areas within the organization.

What We Prefer:

  • (CCM) Certified Case Manager
  • Compact State Licensure in good standing.
  • Prior experience in utilization management or case management preferred, preferably within the managed care environment
  • Intensive care or higher-acuity patient experience preferred. 
  • Knowledge of managed care in a self-funded employer population is preferred. 
  • Ability to identify problems such as underutilization or overutilization of services 
  • Ability to promote and maintain quality care through analysis

What We Can Offer YOU!

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As a WebTPA employee, you will have access to:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, Short- and long-term disability programs
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances
  • Retirement Savings Plan includes employer contribution and employer match
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, and 11 holidays
  • Additional voluntary benefits available and a comprehensive wellness program

Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for interns and part-time employees may differ.

General Physical Demands: 

Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: Claims Examiner I
jobs.description_html:
Get To Know Us!

WebTPA, a GuideWell Company, is a healthcare third-party administrator with over 30+ years of experience building unique benefit solutions and managing customized health plans.

Key position details: 

  • Anticipated Training Class Start Dates:  10/12/2026, 11/9/2026, 12/7/2026
  • Schedule Monday to Friday 8:00am - 4:30pm Central Time for 4 weeks

What is your impact?
As a Claim Examiner, you will handle processing and adjudication for healthcare claims. This will include claims research where applicable and a range of claim complexity. 

What Will You Be Doing: 

The essential functions listed represent the major duties of this role, additional duties may be assigned.

  • Day-to-day processing of claims for accounts:
    • Responsible for processing of claims (medical, dental, vision, and mental health claims)
    • Claims processing and adjudication.
    • Claims research where applicable. 
    • Reviews and processes insurance to verify medical necessities and coverage under policy guidelines (clinical edit logic).
    • Incumbents are expected to meet and/or exceed qualitative and quantitative production standards.
  • Investigation and overpayment administration:
    • Facilitate claims investigation, negotiate settlements, interpret medical records, respond to Department of Insurance complaints, and authorize payment to claimants and providers.
    • Overpayment reviews and recovery of claims overpayment; corrected financial histories of patients and service providers to ensure accurate records.
    • Utilize systems to track complaints and resolutions. 
  • Other responsibilities include resolving claims appeals, researching benefits, verifying correct plan loading. 

What You Must Have: 

  • 2+ years related work experience.
  • Claims examiner/adjudication experience on a computerized claims payment system in the healthcare industry.
  • High school diploma or GED 
  • Knowledge of CPT and ICD-9 coding required. 
  • Knowledge of COBRA, HIPAA, pre-existing conditions, and coordination of benefits required. 
  • Must possess proven judgment, decision-making skills and the ability to analyze. 
  • Ability to learn quickly and multitask.
  • Proficiency in maintaining good rapport with physicians, healthcare facilities, clients and providers. 
  • Concise written and verbal communication skills required, including the ability to handle conflict. 
  • Proficiency using Microsoft Windows and Word, Excel and customized programs for medical CPT coding. 
  • Review of multiple surgical procedures and establishment of reasonable and customary fees.

What We Prefer: 

  • Some college courses in related fields are a plus.
  • Other experience in processing all types of medical claims helpful. 
  • Data entry and 10-key by touch/sight 

What We Can Offer YOU!

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As a WebTPA employee, you will have access to:

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, Short- and long-term disability programs

jobs.title: Enterprise Strategy Principal
jobs.description_html:
The Enterprise Strategy Principal runs a full engagement end to end — scope, plan, team, timeline, and quality — for one of GuideWell’s in-house strategy projects. The Engagement Manager owns the analytic approach and the engagement storyline, balancing rigor against speed, and turns findings into an actionable roadmap that the leaders who must act on it will back. Day to day, they hold the executive-sponsor relationship, manage and develop a team of Associates and Analysts, and are deep enough in one or more segments to anticipate the regulatory and market shifts that could change the answer. This is the first level accountable for a whole project and its outcome: the priority is to deliver engagements that change decisions, and to prepare for Senior Engagement Manager, where scope grows to multiple concurrent engagements or a complex program.

GuideWell is standing up its Enterprise Strategy team — an in-house strategy and internal-consulting group — and we are hiring Engagement Managers to help build it. As an Engagement Manager, you run a full engagement end to end: you scope the problem, set the approach, build and lead the team, own the storyline, and land a recommendation and roadmap that senior leaders act on. You hold the executive-sponsor relationship day to day, and you are accountable for the outcome — the intellectual challenge and variety of consulting, without the constant travel.

You will thrive here if you like owning a whole problem and a whole team, are comfortable sitting across from an executive sponsor and telling them something they may not want to hear, and want your recommendations to be implemented rather than filed.

What makes GuideWell different:

  • A not-for-profit, mission-driven company — one of the nation’s largest health insurers and a Fortune 500 organization — whose purpose is helping people and communities achieve better health.

  • Core Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans in Florida (Florida Blue) and Puerto Rico (Triple-S), with deep ties to government-sponsored health care and the members who rely on it.

  • A diversified portfolio that reaches well beyond insurance — including GuideWell Health care delivery (Sanitas Medical Centers, GuideWell Emergency Doctors, and Florida Health Care Plans), GuideWell Source, WebTPA, and Lucet — serving tens of millions of people across all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

  • A policyholder-owned, long-term orientation and a strong balance sheet that let us invest in health-care-defining capabilities rather than chase quarterly results.

  • Deep community trust and a genuine focus on impact in everything we do.

Why join the team as an Engagement Manager:

  • Own the whole thing — the problem, the plan, the team, and the answer — on questions that matter to a Fortune 500 health company.

  • See your work through to a decision. Because we are in-house, you stay for the roadmap and the follow-through rather than handing off at the final read-out.

  • Build something that lasts — as an early hire you will help set the engagement model, the playbooks, and the standards of a purpose-built team.

  • Grow a full strategy career here, with clear levels, a transparent competency model, and mentorship built into every engagement, all the way to Head of Enterprise Strategy.

  • Or use the team as a launchpad into the business: leadership brokers moves into functional lead and director roles against real openings, with sponsorship and a published leveling equivalence.

If you want to run real strategy work end to end in service of a mission you believe in, and help build the team that does it, we would like to meet you.

Key Requirements

Run a Full Engagement End to End

  • Run a full engagement from start to finish — scope, workplan, team, timeline, and quality — and be accountable for the outcome.

  • Scope the problem with the sponsor, define what is in and out, and reset scope openly when the facts change.

  • Staff and structure the team from the shared pool, allocate the work, and manage pace and capacity across the engagement.

  • Own delivery risk — anticipate what could derail the engagement and act before it does.

Own the Analytic Approach and Balance Rigor Against Speed

  • Own the analytic approach for the whole engagement, deciding which questions get depth and which get a directional answer.

  • Balance rigor against speed deliberately, and be explicit with the sponsor about the trade-off being made.

  • Review and challenge the team’s analysis, and take personal responsibility for the integrity of the numbers.

Own the Storyline, the Roadmap, and the Buy-In

  • Own the engagement storyline, tailoring the message to the audience without softening the conclusion.

  • Turn findings into an actionable roadmap — sequenced moves, owners, and the decisions required to start.

  • Secure the buy-in of the leaders who must act, working the recommendation through in advance rather than unveiling it at the read-out.

Manage and Develop the Engagement Team

  • Manage and develop a team of Associates and Analysts — set direction, give direct feedback, and hold a clear standard.

  • Create the conditions for people to do their best work: clear roles, useful coaching, and protection from unnecessary churn.

  • Drive recruiting and shape how engagements are run, contributing to the team’s playbooks, tools, and onboarding.

Own the Executive-Sponsor Relationship and Deepen Segment Expertise

  • Own the day-to-day executive-sponsor relationship for the engagement, keeping them ahead of both progress and problems.

  • Go deep in one or more segments, and anticipate the regulatory and market shifts that could change the recommendation.

  • Build the cross-functional relationships — business units, finance, corporate development — that the engagement depends on.

Qualifications

  • 7-10 years of experience.

  • 7+ years in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a comparable role, including demonstrated experience leading project teams.

  • Demonstrated experience running projects end to end — scope, workplan, team, timeline, and quality — with accountability for the outcome.

  • Per the team’s leveling map, post-MBA consultants with demonstrated project leadership enter at this level or as a Senior Associate.

Required Management Experience

  • 2+ years leading project teams; formal people-management experience preferred

Required Education

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • Quantitative, analytical, business, or health-related field preferred (e.g., economics, finance, statistics, data or analytics, engineering, or public health); other majors welcome where the analytical toolkit is demonstrated.

Preferred Education

  • MBA or other relevant advanced degree

Additional Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience running projects end to end — scope, plan, team, timeline, and quality — and being accountable for the outcome.

  • The ability to scope an ambiguous problem with a sponsor, define what is in and out, and reset scope openly when the facts change.

  • The ability to own the analytic approach for a whole engagement and to balance rigor against speed deliberately and explicitly.

  • A track record of owning a storyline and turning findings into an actionable roadmap that the leaders who must act on it will back.

  • Experience managing and developing a team, including giving direct feedback and holding a clear standard.

  • The ability to hold a senior-sponsor relationship day to day, including telling a sponsor something they may not want to hear.

  • Executive-level written and verbal communication, and the ability to tailor a message without softening the conclusion.

  • Depth in one or more health care segments, and an eye on the regulatory and market shifts that could change a recommendation.

  • The ability to build the cross-functional relationships — business units, finance, corporate development — that an engagement depends on.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience at engagement-manager level or equivalent at a top-tier strategy consultancy, or comparable in-house strategy leadership.

  • MBA or other relevant advanced degree.

  • Health plan or payer experience.

  • A record of recommendations that were implemented, not just presented.

  • Experience contributing to the playbooks, tools, or onboarding of a strategy team.

  • Recruiting and interviewing experience.

General Physical Demands
Sedentary work: Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally to move objects. Jobs are sedentary if traversing activities are required only occasionally. 
 

Physical/Environmental Activities
Must be able to travel to multiple locations for work (i.e. travel to attend meetings, events, conferences). Occasionally 

What We Offer: 
As a Florida Blue employee, you will be at the heart of GuideWell’s vision – to lead the nation in transforming health through compassionate, connected, and technology-enabled care that delivers personalized value and empowered living. 

To support your wellbeing, comprehensive benefits are offered. As an employee, you will have access to: 
 

  • Medical, dental, vision, life and global travel health insurance;
  • Income protection benefits: life insurance, short- and long-term disability programs;
  • Leave programs to support personal circumstances;
  • Retirement Savings Plan including employer match;
  • Paid time off, volunteer time off, 10 holidays and 2 well-being days;
  • Additional voluntary benefits available; and
  • A comprehensive wellness program


Employee benefits are designed to align with federal and state employment laws. Benefits may vary based on the state in which work is performed. Benefits for intern, part-time and seasonal employees may differ.

To support your financial wellbeing, we offer competitive pay as well as opportunities for incentive or commission compensation. We also conduct regular annual reviews with pay for performance considerations for base pay increases. 

Annualized Salary Range: $126,000 - $204,800

Typical Annualized Hiring Range: $126,000 - $157,500

Final pay will be determined with consideration of market competitiveness, internal equity, and the job-related knowledge, skills, training, and experience you bring.

We are an Equal Employment Opportunity employer committed to cultivating a work experience where everyone feels like they belong and can perform at their best in pursuit of our mission. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment.

jobs.title: Enterprise Strategy Director
jobs.description_html:
The Enterprise Strategy Director is the lead in-house strategy advisor to one of GuideWell’s business segments, partnering directly with its leadership to solve the enterprise’s most important and most complex problems. Operating like an internal engagement lead, the Director owns discrete, time-bound engagements from start to finish — framing the question, directing a small team of analysts, and turning analysis into clear, decision-ready recommendations for senior leaders and, where relevant, the Board. Working across business-unit peers, segment subject-matter experts, finance, and corporate development, the Director connects internal and external insight to sharpen GuideWell’s view of the market dynamics shaping strategy, growth, and operations.

GuideWell is standing up its Enterprise Strategy team — an in-house strategy and internal-consulting group — and we are looking for a Director to help build it from the ground up. You will be the trusted strategy advisor to the leaders of a GuideWell business, own strategic engagements end to end (from framing the problem to delivering the recommendation), and present your thinking directly to senior leadership. Because the team is being purpose-built, you will have unusual influence over how it works: the engagement model, the playbooks and tools, and the analysts you develop along the way.

You will thrive here if you love turning ambiguous, cross-functional problems into clear recommendations, are energized by working shoulder to shoulder with senior leaders, and want the intellectual challenge and variety of consulting without the constant travel — all in service of a mission you believe in.

What makes GuideWell different:

  • A not-for-profit, mission-driven company — one of the nation’s largest health insurers and a Fortune 500 organization — whose purpose is helping people and communities achieve better health.
  • Core Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans in Florida (Florida Blue) and Puerto Rico (Triple-S), with deep ties to government-sponsored health care and the members who rely on it.
  • A diversified portfolio that reaches well beyond insurance — including GuideWell Health care delivery (Sanitas Medical Centers, GuideWell Emergency Doctors, and Florida Health Care Plans), GuideWell Source, WebTPA, and Lucet — serving tens of millions of people across all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
  • A policyholder-owned, long-term orientation and a strong balance sheet that let us invest in health-care-defining capabilities rather than chase quarterly results.
  • Deep community trust and a genuine focus on impact in everything we do.

Why join the Enterprise Strategy team:

  • Build something that lasts. As one of the first Directors, you will help set the engagement model, the standards, and the culture of a purpose-built team, and leave your fingerprints on both the work and the people.
  • Work on problems that matter — helping GuideWell get the whole concept of health care right, not just run a health plan — during a period of real growth and transformation.
  • Grow a full strategy career here, with clear levels, a transparent competency model, and mentorship built into every engagement, all the way to Head of Enterprise Strategy. 
  • Or use the team as a launchpad into the business: at defined points you can move into an operating (P&L or functional) role, supported by optional 6–12 month secondments with a guaranteed path back and sponsored placements that keep the move a step up, never a step down. People who move on stay part of the strategy alumni network — and we count that as a win.

Above all, this is a chance to put sharp strategic thinking behind a mission worth believing in: helping the people and communities we serve achieve better health.

Key Requirements

Own the Strategy Agenda for a Business Segment

  • Own the strategy agenda for an assigned P&L or group of support-services functions, serving as the embedded strategy advisor to that unit’s leadership team.

  • Frame the strategic questions that matter most before the analysis begins, and shape the major bets and investment choices that follow.

  • Translate GuideWell’s enterprise strategy into a clear roadmap for the segment, and keep it current as markets, competitors, and regulation evolve.

  • Act as the single point of accountability for the segment’s strategy work, driving alignment across business partners in a matrixed environment.

Lead Strategic Engagements End to End

  • Run discrete, time-bound engagements from start to finish — scoping the problem, structuring the analysis, and setting the workplan.

  • Direct a team of analysts drawn from the shared team pool, owning quality, pace, and the balance between rigor and speed.

  • Turn analysis into decision-ready recommendations and a practical roadmap, and secure the buy-in of the leaders who must act on it.

  • Present findings directly to business-unit and enterprise leaders, tailoring the message to the audience.

Inform the Executive and Board Strategy Process

  • Provide the data, market intelligence, frameworks, and facilitation that help executives define, align on, and refresh enterprise, business-unit, and functional strategy.

  • Develop scenarios and test current and proposed strategies against them, anticipating how traditional and non-traditional competitors alike could reshape the market.

  • Prepare clear, decision-ready materials for executive leadership and, where relevant, the Board, supporting the enterprise strategy-refresh cycle.

Develop Talent and Build the Practice

  • Coach and develop the analysts staffed to your engagements — setting direction, reviewing their work, and giving direct, timely feedback as part of the Enterprise Strategy team.

  • Strengthen the team’s shared methods, tools, and intellectual property, raising the bar for how engagements are run.

  • Help the team scale by contributing to recruiting and onboarding and by developing the analysts you lead, both directly and indirectly.

Build Cross-Enterprise Relationships and Outside-In Thinking

  • Build durable, trusted relationships with peers across business units, finance, and corporate development, and respond to inbound requests for strategic analysis.

  • Introduce new ideas and frameworks that embed long-term, outside-in thinking into everyday business decisions.

  • Partner with subject-matter experts to assess what federal and state health care legislation, policy, and regulation mean for GuideWell’s strategy.

Qualifications

  • 12-16 years of experience.

  • 12+ years in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a comparable role, including significant experience leading engagements and senior relationships.

  • Demonstrated experience owning the strategy agenda for a business or major function, and advising its leadership team.

  • Per the team’s leveling map, an experienced Engagement Manager, Project Leader, or Manager from a top-tier firm slots in at this level.

Required Management Experience

  • 5+ years leading teams and developing talent, including indirect leadership in a matrixed environment.

Required Education

  • Bachelor’s degree

  • Quantitative, analytical, business, or health-related field preferred (e.g., economics, finance, statistics, data or analytics, engineering, or public health); other majors welcome where the analytical toolkit is demonstrated.

Preferred Education

  • MBA or other relevant advanced degree

  • MBA, or a master’s degree in a quantitative, analytical, business, or health-related field (e.g., economics, finance, statistics, data science, engineering, or public health).

Additional Qualifications

  • Demonstrated experience owning the strategy agenda for a business or major function, including framing the questions before the analysis begins.
  • A track record as a trusted advisor to a leadership team, with real influence over major bets and investment choices.
  • The ability to run engagements end to end while also carrying a standing coverage relationship.
  • The ability to translate an enterprise strategy into a unit-level roadmap, and to keep it current as markets, competitors, and regulation move.
  • Experience preparing and delivering decision-ready material for executive leadership and, where relevant, a Board.
  • The ability to build bench strength — developing talent and sponsoring careers, directly and indirectly.
  • Command of a market: its competitors, its regulation, and the economics that drive it.
  • Executive presence, and the ability to frame strategy in the language of the leaders who have to act on it.
  • The ability to act as a single point of accountability and drive alignment in a matrixed environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience at engagement-manager level or above at a top-tier strategy consultancy, or experience leading an in-house strategy function.
  • MBA or other relevant advanced degree.
  • Deep health care experience; payer experience strongly preferred.
  • Experience with scenario planning and with an enterprise strategy-refresh cycle.
  • Experience with corporate development, M&A, or partnership strategy.
  • Experience building a team’s shared methods, tools, and intellectual property.

Working across business-unit peers, segment subject-matter experts, finance, and corporate development, the Director connects internal and external insight to sharpen GuideWell’s view of the market dynamics shaping strategy, growth, and operations.
 GuideWell is standing up its Enterprise Strategy team — an in-house strategy and internal-consulting group — and we are looking for a Director to help build it from the ground up. You will be the trusted strategy advisor to the leaders of a GuideWell business, own strategic engagements end to end (from framing the problem to delivering the recommendation), and present your thinking directly to senior leadership. Because the team is being purpose-built, you will have unusual influence over how it works: the engagement model, the playbooks and tools, and the analysts you develop along the way.
 You will thrive here if you love turning ambiguous, cross-functional problems into clear recommendations, are energized by working shoulder to shoulder with senior leaders, and want the intellectual challenge and variety of consulting without the constant travel — all in service of a mission you believe in.
 What makes GuideWell different:
 A not-for-profit, mission-driven company — one of the nation’s largest health insurers and a Fortune 500 organization — whose purpose is helping people and communities achieve better health.
 Core Blue Cross Blue Shield health plans in Florida (Florida Blue) and Puerto Rico (Triple-S), with deep ties to government-sponsored health care and the members who rely on it.
 A diversified portfolio that reaches well beyond insurance — including GuideWell Health care delivery (Sanitas Medical Centers, GuideWell Emergency Doctors, and Florida Health Care Plans), GuideWell Source, WebTPA, and Lucet — serving tens of millions of people across all 50 states, Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands.
 A policyholder-owned, long-term orientation and a strong balance sheet that let us invest in health-care-defining capabilities rather than chase quarterly results.
 Deep community trust and a genuine focus on impact in everything we do.
 Why join the Enterprise Strategy team:
 Build something that lasts. As one of the first Directors, you will help set the engagement model, the standards, and the culture of a purpose-built team, and leave your fingerprints on both the work and the people.
 Work on problems that matter — helping GuideWell get the whole concept of health care right, not just run a health plan — during a period of real growth and transformation.
 Grow a full strategy career here, with clear levels, a transparent competency model, and mentorship built into every engagement, all the way to Head of Enterprise Strategy. 
 Or use the team as a launchpad into the business: at defined points you can move into an operating (P&L or functional) role, supported by optional 6–12 month secondments with a guaranteed path back and sponsored placements that keep the move a step up, never a step down. People who move on stay part of the strategy alumni network — and we count that as a win.
 Above all, this is a chance to put sharp strategic thinking behind a mission worth believing in: helping the people and communities we serve achieve better health.
 Key Requirements 
 Own the Strategy Agenda for a Business Segment
 Own the strategy agenda for an assigned P&L or group of support-services functions, serving as the embedded strategy advisor to that unit’s leadership team.
 Frame the strategic questions that matter most before the analysis begins, and shape the major bets and investment choices that follow.
 Translate GuideWell’s enterprise strategy into a clear roadmap for the segment, and keep it current as markets, competitors, and regulation evolve.
 Act as the single point of accountability for the segment’s strategy work, driving alignment across business partners in a matrixed environment.
 Lead Strategic Engagements End to End
 Run discrete, time-bound engagements from start to finish — scoping the problem, structuring the analysis, and setting the workplan.
 Direct a team of analysts drawn from the shared team pool, owning quality, pace, and the balance between rigor and speed.
 Turn analysis into decision-ready recommendations and a practical roadmap, and secure the buy-in of the leaders who must act on it.
 Present findings directly to business-unit and enterprise leaders, tailoring the message to the audience.
 Inform the Executive and Board Strategy Process
 Provide the data, market intelligence, frameworks, and facilitation that help executives define, align on, and refresh enterprise, business-unit, and functional strategy.
 Develop scenarios and test current and proposed strategies against them, anticipating how traditional and non-traditional competitors alike could reshape the market.
 Prepare clear, decision-ready materials for executive leadership and, where relevant, the Board, supporting the enterprise strategy-refresh cycle.
 Develop Talent and Build the Practice
 Coach and develop the analysts staffed to your engagements — setting direction, reviewing their work, and giving direct, timely feedback as part of the Enterprise Strategy team.
 Strengthen the team’s shared methods, tools, and intellectual property, raising the bar for how engagements are run.
 Help the team scale by contributing to recruiting and onboarding and by developing the analysts you lead, both directly and indirectly.
 Build Cross-Enterprise Relationships and Outside-In Thinking
 Build durable, trusted relationships with peers across business units, finance, and corporate development, and respond to inbound requests for strategic analysis.
 Introduce new ideas and frameworks that embed long-term, outside-in thinking into everyday business decisions.
 Partner with subject-matter experts to assess what federal and state health care legislation, policy, and regulation mean for GuideWell’s strategy.

 12+ years in management consulting, corporate strategy, or a comparable role, including significant experience leading engagements and senior relationships.
 Demonstrated experience owning the strategy agenda for a business or major function, and advising its leadership team.
 Per the team’s leveling map, an experienced Engagement Manager, Project Leader, or Manager from a top-tier firm slots in at this level.
